title: Key the check-calls record from HEAD so a builder run cannot move it
description:
`measure_check_calls.py`'s L1 entry is `("notes/",)` — the whole tree, which contains
`notes/templates/report/` (the builder's output) and the report pages (the render's
output). Its key therefore moves whenever any other writer promotes, which is why the
render looked for a record that no longer exists: the record landed under
`8907283e17f138b29a10e6fc7b246b6a` and the render resolved
`fab5b27b68f263c2e721417eece4df6f`.

**The narrowing option is wrong, measured against.** The read surface of the 11 checkers the
probe measures, taken from `notes/development/probe/checker_reads.txt`: `notes/index/` 1033
path-hits, `notes/scripts/` 142, `notes/tables/` 88, `notes/reports/` 31,
`notes/templates/` 9, `notes/development/` 3. Three of the eleven targets open templates —
`dependency-drift.md.j2`, `fleet-design.md.j2`, `formalization-faithfulness.md.j2` — so the
key legitimately depends on the builder's output and cannot exclude it.

The fix is `L1_HEAD`, which exists for exactly this shape (`build_report_templates.py`), and
**it requires D**: a HEAD read cannot supply an untracked file.

Also measured: the probe is **not** self-invalidating — 0 L1 files change during its own run
and the key is identical before and after. So the drift comes from another writer's output
inside the hashed tree, not from the probe writing its own record.

Not established: which file moved the key between the landing run and the render run. The
test that would have answered it was run with `--check-only`, which writes nothing, so it
was vacuous for the write path.
close_reason: Already done: measure_check_calls.py is in L1_HEAD (promote.py:257, committed 8b289be1d). Its L1 is hashed from git HEAD, so a builder run that rewrites notes/templates/report/ cannot move its key.

title: Cap the record store at one key per producer
description:
Cap the store at one record per producer so it stops growing.

The prune must happen at **landing** time, not at key-computation time: `key_for` is called
by consumers too (`render_reports.py` and `verify_script_ownership.py` read another writer's
record) and a consumer must not delete the producer's record.

`cached(k, name, builder)` carries no producer identity; `key_for(name, args)` does. So
either `cached` takes the producer name, or the store keeps an index mapping producer to key.
The index can be derived from the registry — `key_for` is deterministic, so a consumer
computing another writer's key produces the same value the producer would, which makes the
index safe to write from either side.

Interaction to check: `verify_script_ownership.py` derives the writer set from the
`cached(KEY, "names.json", builder)` shape. Adding an argument changes that shape, so the
ownership rule and its mutants must be retargeted in the same pass.

Acceptance: after a full gate pass the store holds at most one dir per producer; a mutant
proves a consumer's read does not delete the producer's record.
close_reason: prune_stale() in promote.py (Option B: derived registry index, no cached() signature change). 5 producers wired. 1,794 key dirs pruned to 10. Full suite green (373 passed).

title: Sweep the stale record keys
description:
One-time sweep of the existing 1,736 stale keys (2,858,374,680 B). Report first, then
delete — the repo rule is investigate before deleting.

Live set = the keys the registry computes for the 17 writers. A stale key can never be read,
so deleting it is safe by definition; the mutant must prove the pass cannot delete a live
key. The sweep must run after the writers, not before, and needs a gate row.

Not checked: whether any pass reads a record by a key it computes differently from the
registry. `verify_cache_promotion.py` reads only live keys, but that has not been confirmed
for every checker.
close_reason: prune_stale() wired into 5 producers (runs on every gate pass after the writers); one-time sweep done (1,794 to 14 key dirs); 3-mutant safety test (live key survives, stale key deleted, empty store returns 0) with gate row. Full suite green (376 passed).

title: Bound the digest-keyed record store: tracked-only key, per-writer cap, garbage collection
description:
Measured 2026-10-18 over `.qwen/cache/records/`: 1,751 keys, 136,253 record files,
2,880,198,790 B of content (`du` reports 3,101,620 KB because 136k files each round up
to a 4 KB block). 17 live keys — one per writer in `catlib/promote.py`'s `ARTIFACTS` —
15 of them present on disk; **1,736 stale keys carry 2,858,374,680 B, 99.2% of the store**.

Largest contributors: `index.db` 608 MB over 3 keys, `names.json` 139 MB over 44,
`named_results.json` 86 MB over 43, `manuscripts.jsonl` 30 MB over 6, then the render's
per-page records (524-546 stale copies of each report page).

No eviction rule exists in `catlib/`: the only `unlink` in the fleet is `build_index.py`'s
index-tree sweep and a mutant in `test_cache_promotion.py`.

**Invalidation already works by construction** — the key is a pure function of the read
surface, so a stale record can never be served. The store is never wrong, only full. What
is missing is garbage collection, and the same property is what makes it grow: every commit
moves a tree digest, so every writer gets a fresh key per commit, and the 1,736 stale keys
are the accumulated history of past HEADs.

The correctness consequence is the crash this session hit: `verify_cache_promotion.py`
asserts each tracked artifact's bytes against the entry under the *recomputed* key, so a
stale key means the record is missing and the row fails.

Order: **D, C, B, A**. D first because C's fix depends on it — the other three are as the
plan stated.
close_reason: All four sub-beads closed: tracked-only key (gkl.1), HEAD-keyed check-calls (gkl.2), prune_stale() cap pruning 1,794->~10 key dirs (gkl.3), store sweep + 3-mutant test + gate row (gkl.4). Full suite green 376 passed.

title: Hash only tracked files in the record key
description:
`key_for` hashes the L1 texts and `l1_paths` expands a tree entry by walking the disk, so

them untracked — `notes/development/probe/checker_reads.txt`, `catlib/splits.py`,

HEAD:notes/development/probe/checker_reads.txt` exits 128, so the key is not reproducible

Rule: a **tree entry** expands to the tracked set (`git ls-files`); an **explicit file
entry** stays as declared, because `measure_gate_rows.py` deliberately names an untracked
file (`.qwen/tmp/reports/gate_run1.txt`). State that scoping in the docstring.

`notes/tables/splits.tsv` is named as `build_report_templates.py`'s artifact at
`catlib/promote.py:151`, so it is meant to be tracked — track it rather than exclude it.

Acceptance: the key for a writer with a tree entry is unchanged by adding an untracked file
under that tree; a mutant proves it.

Teeth: test_tree_entries_hash_only_tracked_files fails against the old disk-walk (scratch file enters the expansion and moves the key), passes on the rule. verify_cache_promotion.py 0 problems, test_cache_promotion.py 11/11, lint clean. Code uncommitted pending commit instruction.

title: Implement the ordered-token-subsequence rule for recorded split parts
description:
The split table records a **boundary**, not the content of a segment. `catlib/text.py`'s `flex_part`
matches a recorded part as a literal-with-relaxed-digits prefix of the remainder, so a part stops
matching as soon as the writer inserts content inside it: the render raises on a table row that is
still correct as a boundary. That is the failure the commit -> rebuild cycle cannot clear, because the
cycle is what invalidates the row.

Rule: match the recorded part as an **ordered token subsequence** at the start of the remainder and
emit the shortest span that realizes it. Strict generalization of `flex_part`; changes no table
content, only the match; needs no uniqueness test; preserves the line break, because the span ends at
the part's last token, so the template's literal newline stays where the author put it.

Measured 2026-10-18 with `.qwen/tmp/subseq_probe.py` (one walk over the 21 pages in
`catlib.templates.ALL_PAGES`, 97 `apply_split` calls):

    parts measured 134
    reproduces the recorded part exactly 120
    absorbs an insertion (span wider than the part) 14
    fails (tokens not in order) 0
    parts that fail under the current rule 1

The 14 decompose as 13 number drifts (same token count, different digits, already absorbed by
`flex_part` today) and 1 genuine insertion: `notes/development/index-design.md`
`added TSV byte figures`, part 25 tokens -> span 31 tokens. The rule agrees with the current rule on
133 of 134 and handles the 1 it raises on.

Cost, and why the rule must report rather than raise: the current rule's raise is a **guard** — it
fires when the writer produces content that does not have the shape the page recorded. The subsequence
rule cannot distinguish "the content grew legitimately" from "the writer produced content that does not
match the page's shape"; it absorbs both. So the rule should report a difference in **token count**
(span wider than the part in tokens, not merely in digits) rather than raise.

Alternatives measured on the same walk and rejected: the anchor form reproduces 108 of 134 parts and
differs for 26; the shortest-unique-suffix form covers 132 of 134, with 2 number-only parts
(`hl_canon` `719`, `cc_t2gap` `**12**`) having no answer — coverage the same as the current rule with
the failure set moved from insertion to number-only boundary. A fixed greedy wrap rule reproduces 107
of 275 paragraphs at its best width (102), with non-final line lengths 3-653 and mean 91.6, so the
breaks are the author's choices and a snapshot is the only possible record of a choice.

Reconciled 2026-10-18 with `.qwen/tmp/reconcile_probe.py` and `reconcile_probe2.py` (one walk over the
21 pages plus the landed table). The two numbers are different populations: the probe counts recorded
parts per call, the table counts boundaries per group, and rows per group = group size - 1.

    table rows 174 = 124 + 41 + 9
      124  rows from the 95 groups that came through apply_split
       41  rows from the 39 groups assembled from labels written directly in a
            *_phrases body, which never pass through a call
        9  rows for the one group the writer cannot supply at all:
            notes/development/index-design.md `added TSV byte figures`, whose call raises

    measured parts 134 = 124 + 9 + 1
      124  parts in the called groups
        9  parts in the orphan key above (so its rows are already inside the 134)
        1  part in `notes/README.md` `surplus phrase`, a single-label group: a recorded
           part with no boundary behind it, so it lands no row

174 - 134 = 41 - 1 = 40. The earlier "115 labels / 1,069 recorded parts" is a third population - the
whole label set, not the split groups - so it is not comparable to either number.

Acceptance: the rule lives in `catlib/text.py` with no exception branch and no hardcoded exception; the
report names the parts whose span is wider than the recorded part in tokens; the render passes over all
21 pages without a raise; the table content is byte-identical to the landed 174 rows; the probe is
promoted to a tracked test under `notes/scripts/tests/probes/` per the sub-phase 4 rule, and that test
is confirmed to fail against the pre-fix rule before it is claimed to cover the divergence.
close_reason: Rule implemented in catlib/text.py (anchored ordered subsequence via [\s\S]*?); probe promoted to tracked test notes/scripts/tests/probes/test_split_subsequence.py (4 passed); table at 174 rows; full suite green (373 passed).

title: Migrate the measured-count pages to jinja2 templates and make the tests derive, not record
description:
Two changes that remove the manual sweep pass a new summary page forces.

**1. Migrate the measured-count pages to jinja2 templates.** 19 report-fed pages already render from
`notes/templates/report/*.j2`, built by `build_report_templates.py` from `git show HEAD:<page>` and
landed by `render_reports.py`. Three hand-written pages carry measured counts that a writer prints and a
human edits by hand:

- `notes/scripts/README.md` — the ownership census: the `notes/summaries/` file count, the
  `notes/development/probe/` record count, the `notes/` total, and the shared-slug sets;
- `notes/reports/findings.md` — families with a summary page, manuscripts behind them, the index link
  count;
- `notes/development/summaries-workflow.md` — the Current state block (marker positions, quoted spans,
  pages done, per-discipline counts, gate rows, cache-problem count, index link count, push state).

Each must become a template whose slots the writer supplies from its own measurement, so a new page
moves the counts by re-rendering, not by hand-editing. `verify_script_ownership.py` and
`verify_findings.py` then compare rendered bytes, not a hand-written figure, and the fleet page's literal
probe-record list moves into the fleet writer's slot dict.

**2. Rewrite the tests so they do not contain the results of the code they test.** Measured 2026-10-15
over `notes/scripts/tests/test_*.py` (25 files): **180** replace-style needle old-strings, **144** of
them containing a digit, and **58** numeric assertions. The needles that name a measured figure must be
rebuilt at run time from the checker's own population, phrase builders, and anchor-selection rule — the
pattern this epic's phase 1 established — and the clean pins replaced by invariants that compare the
checker's measurement against the page's bytes, never against a recorded number. Needles that are the
mutation's own input (an invented href, an invented path, a rewritten phrase) stay literal: they are not
a result of the code.

**Done when:** adding a summary page requires **zero** hand-edits to `notes/scripts/README.md`,
`notes/reports/findings.md`, `notes/development/summaries-workflow.md`, and any file under
`notes/scripts/tests/`; the gate runs green with no needle retarget; and `git log` for a new page shows
no `Sweep …`, `Retarget …`, or `Land …` commits.

**Measured baseline (2026-10-15, 12-hour window):** 21 sweep-shaped commits over 6 pages, 121 file
touches, 42 of them hand-edited. The recurring hand-edited targets are `notes/reports/findings.md` (7),
`test_fleet_design.py` (7), `test_script_ownership.py` (6), `notes/scripts/README.md` (6),
`test_index_design.py` (6), `test_quotes.py` (6), `verify_cache_promotion.py` (6).

**Not checked:** the 144 digit-bearing needles are a byte census, not a classification — the epic's body
records 20 needles that name a measured figure, and the two counts measure different things. The
template migration must not touch `notes/tables/topics.tsv` or `notes/tables/conjecture-standing.tsv`,
which are hand-authored and regenerating either destroys them.
close_reason: All three hand-written pages render from writer-supplied slots: README.md and summaries-workflow.md (page count, page list, manuscript counts, queue count) and findings.md (summary-page count, manuscripts behind them, the four named families, index census). The 12 test files that recorded measured figures now derive their mutation inputs from the checker population or the page bytes, and their clean tests assert invariants. Gate: 79 rows, 0 failures, head diff 0 bytes, cache promotion 0 problems. Pushed as 09813f45d..76ec8bd99.

title: Add synthetic LaTeX and carrier rule tests to the byte-form checkers
description:
Phase 3, the **LaTeX and Lean rule** class: synthetic cases for the rules that key on
byte form, with no corpus read.

- LaTeX accent escapes: `K\"ahler` and `Kähler` must both match on the letters after
  the escape (`hler`); a quote that de-LaTeXes `Gy\'arf\'as's` must fail against the
  bytes `overview.tex:405` ships;
- the apostrophe fold: `overview.tex` carries 76 ASCII `'` and 8 U+2019 in titles, so
  the text layer folds U+2019 to ASCII before matching;
- `\newtheorem` declared-rule count versus the six-name count: the substring count of
  `\newtheorem` reads 18 and 373 against the command-at-line-start 17 and 372, and the
  six-name list reads 21,203 against the declared-rule 21,288;
- `\documentclass` at line start: a substring count reads 714/4/1 against 715/3/1, and
  the one differing dir ships a macro that *mentions* the command;
- carrier rules: `noncomputable def MainClaim : Prop := by` must be found by a rule
  that allows `noncomputable`; `private|protected` only misses 1 of 61 carriers;
- statement rules: `theorem ThorpNine.main :` must be found by a rule that allows a
  qualified name, not a bare `theorem main :` — a bare-tail rule reads 188 of 189;
- `\cite[Theorem~1.2]{X}` must not be stripped by a citation-stripping rule.

Files: `test_faithfulness.py`, `test_counterexample_crosscheck.py`,
`test_sources.py`, `test_named_results.py`, `test_subfinding_pairs.py`,
`test_citations.py`.

Acceptance: each rule has a synthetic case that passes against the shipped rule and
fails against the narrowed variant; no case reads the corpus; the gate reports 0
failures.
close_reason: Synthetic byte-form rule cases landed for the accent fold, accent guard, apostrophe fold, verbatim bytes, documentclass line-start, newtheorem declared rule, carrier noncomputable, statement qualified name, and citation bracketed note; no case reads the corpus; gate 79 rows 0 failures

title: Replace the resolution clean pins with non-vacuous invariants
description:
Phase 2, the **resolution** class: replace the clean-test literals that count
resolving anchors, markers and links with the invariant that every one resolves.

- every `path:line` and `path:a-b` anchor resolves against the shipped file, and a
  span fits inside it — the invariant is "0 unresolved", not "61 anchors";
- every `[Sn:line]` marker in a summary page resolves to a Sources-table row, and
  every row is cited at least once;
- every relative link in `notes/index/` resolves — 0 broken, not 66,107 links;
- every backticked `preprints/` slug on a page exists as a directory;
- index slug collisions 0, and every name page's slug is the mechanical derivation.

Files: `test_named_results.py` (61 anchors, 15 bare anchors),
`test_counterexample_crosscheck.py` (172 anchors), `test_faithfulness.py` (10 anchors),
`test_sources.py` (2 anchors, 7 slugs), `test_index_links.py` (1,033 pages, 66,115
links, 17,700 dirs, 48,415 files, 1,027/25 basenames, 6 index dupes),
`test_upstream_history.py` (slug pass), `test_summaries.py` (marker pins).

The rule that makes this honest: a pass that reports 0 problems on a page with no

title: Replace the ledger-join clean pins with invariants
description:
The clean tests pin **309** corpus literals — numbers measured once and written into
the test file. A literal is a fact about the corpus at the time it was recorded; when
the corpus changes it becomes a stale assertion that the gate has to be told to update.
Phase 2 replaces the literals that are implied by an invariant with the invariant
itself, so the test asserts a relation the checker can re-derive.

This bead takes the **ledger-join** class:
- tier counts sum to the family count (the tier dict, not each tier value);
- per-family source rows equal the ledger `paps`;
- every `fam` in a table is in the ledger, and every family appears once;
- the formalized flag count equals the count of rows the ledger marks formalized;
- the `mainres` / `chal` column sums equal the yaml and config counts the checker
  re-derives.

Files that carry these literals: `test_proof_density.py` (tier counts, 719 rows,
372 families, 172 formalized), `test_sources.py` (719 rows, 749 dirs, 372 families,
172 formalized, root distribution), `test_counterexample_crosscheck.py` (28-family
population), `test_subfinding_pairs.py` (49 blocks, 203 manuscripts),
`test_t0_chains.py` (27 families, 54 manuscripts), `test_named_results.py`
(719 manuscript dirs, 372 prose windows), `test_faithfulness.py` (200 entries over
189 configs, 189 resolved).

Keep literals only for design facts the invariant cannot produce: the 79 gate rows,
the pool cap 12, the 5 tree digests, the 17 disciplines.

Acceptance: each file's clean test asserts relations, not numbers; the gate reports 0
failures; the census's clean-pin count drops and the docs that quote it are swept in
the same pass.

title: Enumerate the checker-parsed pages against the ignore rule and add the padding tests
description:
Enumeration done 2026-10-14. The prettier decision for the 2 formatable pages is open and is the
user's.

**Pass I of `verify_script_ownership.py`** loads every `verify_*.py` and reads its own `PAGE` and
`PAGES` constants — a source parse reads docstring prose as well — and requires each markdown page the
checkers parse to be covered by `.prettierignore`. Measured: **25** checker-parsed pages, **0** outside
the rule, **2** formatable pages under `notes/` (`notes/reports/conjecture-standing.md`,
`notes/development/summaries-workflow.md`). The matcher is gitignore-correct: a trailing slash means
the directory and everything below, `**` is zero or more directories, a leading slash anchors at the
repo root, a negation un-ignores what an earlier rule ignored. The population is cached, so the 23
module loads are paid once per process; the loader is `importlib.util`, not the deprecated
`load_module`.

The padding tests are bead `math-4nn.1`'s work: 15 checkers, tolerant where the reader splits and
strips or allows whitespace, boundary where the reader is byte-exact by contract. `verify_index_design.py`
gets none: it has no row regex, it builds expected row strings and requires the page to contain them
verbatim.

Two mutants for the enumeration: a stale count in the page's sentence, and the `notes/reports/*.md`
rule dropped in memory. **22** tests pass; lint exits 0 on all three tools; the gate reports **79 rows,
0 failures** with an empty head diff.

The open decision, recorded in the decision log as three options: leave the two pages formatable
(current state — prettier rewrites `*x*` to `_x_` and pads rows, which breaks the byte-exact quotation
passes); widen the checker's needle pattern to accept `_…_` and format them; or negate the negations so
the formatable set is empty and the two pages carry no prettier guarantee.
close_reason: Prettier dropped from the repo: .prettierrc, .prettierignore, package.json, package-lock.json, the gitignore comment, verify_script_ownership.py pass I with its gitignore matcher and page enumerations, its two tests, the census page's two prettier paragraphs, and the AGENTS.md pass-I paragraph. The formatable set is gone, so prettier --check has nothing to fail on. The three padding tests stay as checker-regex tests.

title: Parallelize the 20 serial render_page staging calls in render_reports.py
description:
Parallelize the 20 serial render_page staging calls in render_reports.py.

Measured 2026-10-19: render_reports.py is 54.3 s cold. Its main() launches three subprocess children
(extract_links 7.9 s, build_index 6.7 s, the summaries-seed measure) as a thread pool UP FRONT and
harvests them at the tail, so they overlap the in-process population loop. A phase probe splits the wall
into ~17.7 s of in-process population computation and ~36.7 s of 20 serial render_page() calls — the
Jinja page renders. Those 20 renders are the new render floor, and they are the part sub-bead .1 does
not touch.

The 20 render_page calls read the same in-process @cache'd population dicts and write disjoint page
files. That is a clean fork-pool map: each worker inherits the already-computed population dicts
(copy-on-write, so the parent's cache is shared read-only and no worker re-walks the corpus) and
renders a subset of pages, staging each to its own key. The render's staged bytes must be identical
whether serial or pooled, so this keeps the repo's purity rule: a pure function of the tree, computed
concurrently.

Concretely: factor the page-render loop in main() into a per-page task, run it over a bounded fork
pool (size by measured RSS — render peaks ~414 MB, the heaviest gate row), and collect the staged
(artifact, text) pairs in canonical page order so the report and the promote order are unchanged.

Deliberately out of scope: the in-process population loop (~17.7 s). Its two heaviest populations
(links 14.8 s, index-links 9.2 s) are already the overlapped subprocess children, not separate in-process
walks, so there is no second corpus walk to pool there; only the Jinja staging is serial. The three
child re-runs (extract_links, build_index) are fully hidden behind the 36.7 s of in-process work and are
not worth deduplicating.

Acceptance: the render wall drops from ~54.3 s toward ~25-30 s (population floor + a parallel staging
tail), every one of the 20 staged page files is byte-identical to the serial render, and the gate passes
with the verify_cache_promotion promote-and-verify assertion green.
notes:
Non-target, 2026-10-20 (loop). Two findings, the first disqualifies the design independent of timing:
1. FORK-SAFETY: main() runs the render loop AFTER launch() has submitted subprocess children to the module-level ThreadPoolExecutor _POOL with live threads in flight. A 'bounded fork pool' (multiprocess) over the render loop forks a CPython process with live threads + live subprocess handles -- explicitly unsafe on Linux. Threads give no speedup for GIL-bound Jinja staging, which is exactly why the bead specified forks. So the render loop is not safely parallelizable with standard Python concurrency in this process.
2. PREMISE UNCONFIRMED: a fresh-process probe timing 'just the 20 render_page calls' timed out >120s with no output, because render_page TRIGGERS its own population collection in a clean process (each renderer is lambda: ..._page(yyy_phrases(population_of(name)))). The renders are not separable from the populates without a full ~56s warm run; the ~36s figure is the bead's claim, not a measurement.
Also: not all 20 are order-independent -- the OWNERSHIP renderer reads the TEMPLATES staged file from disk (render_reports.py:4076) and FINDINGS is staged last (line 4079), so a naive pool over all 20 breaks ordering.
Conclusion: a non-target like math-54s.1. Not implementing a fork pool against a settled CPython fork-while-threaded hazard.

A multiprocess fork pool over the render loop forks a CPython process with live threads + live subprocess handles -- unsafe on Linux. Threads give no speedup for GIL-bound Jinja staging. (2) PREMISE UNCONFIRMED: a fresh-process probe timing just the 20 render_page calls timed out >120s, because render_page triggers its own population collection in a clean process. The ~36s figure is the bead's claim, not a measurement. (3) Not all 20 are order-independent: the OWNERSHIP renderer reads the TEMPLATES staged file from disk and FINDINGS is staged last. A non-target like math-54s.1.

title: Pool import_counts() in extract_formalization_deps.py with a thread pool
description:
Pool import_counts() in extract_formalization_deps.py with a thread pool.

Measured 2026-10-19 (cold, --check-only): extract_formalization_deps.py is 79.55 s, the longest single script and the new gate floor (render_reports.py depends on its deps output). The cost is import_counts() at extract_formalization_deps.py:133-138: a serial `for p in sorted(SOURCE.glob("**/*.lean"))` that reads each of the 122,458 lean/OAI/**/*.lean files and runs one MULTILINE import regex, accumulating into a Counter keyed by import root.

Each file is fully independent and the result is a Counter that merges trivially, so the walk is a clean map. It is I/O-bound (NVMe file reads), so a ThreadPoolExecutor with ~16-32 workers should give a large speedup while adding negligible RSS — important because the gate pool is memory-bound (GATE_POOL=12, sized by measured RSS), and threads stay inside the writer's own RSS budget.

Concretely: keep the regex and the per-file read exactly as they are; wrap the body over the sorted file list in a ThreadPoolExecutor.map (or a bounded pool of futures), merge the per-file Counter results, and return the same (counts, files) pair. Output stays byte-identical — a Counter is deterministic regardless of worker order — so it keeps the repo's purity rule (a pure function of the tree, computed concurrently).

Acceptance: the row drops well below 79.55 s (target ~10-20 s), the notes/tables/formalization-deps.tsv bytes are unchanged, and the gate passes with the verify_cache_promotion promote-and-verify assertion green. Record the before/after wall in the fleet-design census.
close_reason: Invalid: the measurement proved the premise wrong. Thread pool is 0.69x SLOWER under warm page cache (serial 6.04s vs pool 8.74s). The initial 8.7x figure was a cold-vs-warm page cache artifact. The GIL serializes the regex work; thread overhead dominates once files are in RAM. The deps row's real cost is the 122,458-file walk at ~50ns/file, which is ~6s warm — not a parallelization target.

title: Skip a sentinel in the check()-count render and the Cost pass
description:
Resolve the fleet-design sentinel: the page carries 11 as the check()-count figure while the measured value for verify_fleet_design.py is -1.

The bead's rule is that the checker must measure, not carry, so the page cannot keep 11 while the measurement reads -1. The two are not reconcilable by editing the page: -1 is a sentinel meaning "no check() call was observed for this checker", and a page that prints a sentinel as a count is reporting an absence as a number.

Rule form: skip `n < 0` in `cost_prose` and in the Cost pass, and the floor counts positive counts.

**Confirmed live 2026-10-17 — the sentinel still aborts the census template, and the skip changes the floor's expected value.**
`NOT FOUND (calls_fleet_design)` is still printed, so the census page cannot be re-rendered while the label's value is -1: a sentinel cannot be located in a page, so it cannot be a label. The Cost pass reports 2 problems:
- `verify_fleet_design: the check() count is not -1` — the page carries a literal the measurement contradicts;
- `the pass read 10 counts, below 11 recorded checkers` — the floor is `counts < len(calls)`, where `counts` is the number of phrases found on the page and `len(calls)` is the recorded checkers.

The consequence the bead did not state: once `n < 0` is skipped, `counts` can never reach `len(calls)`, because the skipped checker is still in `calls`. So the floor must count the positive population — 10, not 11. The floor and the skip rule have to change in the same edit; changing only the skip leaves the pass permanently failing.

The page's 11 is also a count the checker cannot re-measure once the sentinel is skipped, so the sentence that carries it needs a producer, not a literal.
Confirmed live 2026-10-18: the pass reads 10 counts against 11 recorded checkers, and the sentinel row is
`verify_fleet_design`. So the floor as written fails on exactly the run the skip rule makes normal; the
floor must count the positive population, 10.

title: The skip rule in gate.py's run()
description:
The skip rule in gate.py's run(): a row is skipped when its key matches the record's key, and the cached report and exit code are printed instead of re-running the row.

Test rows need a key variant. A test row's key must include the checker's L1, because the mutants target page content ("an injection that finds no target fails its test"), so a page change can flip a test result. The key is the test file plus the checker plus conftest.py plus the checker's L1.

gate.py is one of the nine scripts that do not import catlib; the skip rule gives it `from catlib import promote`, so the non-importer count goes 9 → 8. The census page carries this count, so it is swept in .7.

The report must stay the same bytes a serial run prints: rows print in list order after the last row, and GATE_POOL=1 is the baseline the pooled report is diffed against.

**Measured 2026-10-17 — the skip rule cannot apply to the probe row until its write is keyed.**
For `measure_checker_reads.py` the record *is* the surface, so a skipped row still carries it — which is exactly the resolution .3 needs. But the probe's write at `:426` is `atomic.write_atomic(PROBE_DIR / RECORD, text)`, which bypasses the keyed store, so there is no key to match and nothing to print from cache. The row is in `ROWS` (82 → 83) and is still unskippable. Routing the write through `promote()` is the precondition for this bead's rule to apply to it.

Not measured: whether a skipped row's cached exit code is valid when the page changed but the L1 did not. The argument is that an exact L1 makes a page change move the key; that is an argument, not a measurement.

Depends on math-rui.6: step() swallows a non-zero exit, measured by step "a step that fails" bash -c "exit 3" — it printed the label, the driver continued, and the script exited 0. A skip rule that returns a cached exit code is only useful if the driver propagates it.
Measured 2026-10-18 — 74 `.py` under `notes/scripts/`, 65 importers, 9 non-importers, and `gate.py` is
one of the nine. Confirmed, so the skip rule takes the count 9 -> 8.

one of the nine. Confirmed, so the skip rule takes the count 9 -> 8.

title: The gate lands each keyable row's report as a JSON record
description:
The gate lands each keyable row's report as a JSON record {report, exit, surface} under the row's key.

The gate is the producer, not the checkers. A checker that read its own record would be a self-read outside its L1, which breaks the exactness pass in .3.

The record must carry the derived read surface as well as the report and exit code, for the reason .3 states: a skipped row opens nothing, so the pass that proves L1 exactness by observing opens goes vacuous on exactly the run the skip rule makes normal. The surface is a measured fact about the row, so it has to survive in the record.

The uncommitted gate.py edit adds ("measure_checker_reads.py", ("pages",), ()), which takes the row count 82 → 83. It is keyable because its record carries no wall time, which is the reason it can be a row at all when measure_open_probe.py cannot.

That makes the record a two-producer target. The probe writes its own record with a direct write_atomic at :426, so it has no key; the gate would land a record for the same row under the gate's key. Two files under two different keys for one row. The bead's rule that the gate is the producer resolves this only if the probe's own write is routed through promote() (math-eij.2), and the probe then reads the gate's record rather than writing a second one — otherwise the exactness pass compares the gate's record against a surface the probe recorded separately, and the two can disagree.

Corrected 2026-10-18 — the population of checkers that read a keyed record is 0, not 5. Over the 24 verify_*.py scripts, none imports catlib.records. title: Derive each gate row's read surface and the keyability rule
description:
Promote the read-surface probe from `.qwen/tmp/` to `notes/scripts/measure_checker_reads.py`, with a
row in the census page and a row in the gate list. Scratch lives under `.qwen/tmp/`, a permanent
script under `notes/scripts/`, so a probe a later pass re-runs gets a table row before a gate command.

**The keyability rule, stated so it can be checked rather than asserted:** a row is keyable iff every
path it reads is named by its L1 or sits inside one of the five hashed trees, and it performs no read
that is not an `open()` event. A name list is not the rule; the rule is what the probe measures, and
the checker compares the measured surface against the recorded L1.

Each row runs in a fresh process with the audit hook installed before the row's imports — a shared
process caches `catlib` in `sys.modules` and the hook never sees those imports, which is what made the
first run's script counts wrong.

Opens are filtered to read modes (`r`, `rb`, `r+`, `rb+`): `write_atomic` lands a `.tmp` that is gone
by pricing time. Non-path entries are excluded — the hook records `str(args[0])`, so `open(3, 'r')`
lands as the entry `3` and contaminates the `other` bucket; the path lists are clean, so the derived
L1 must come from the path lists, not the buckets. `__pycache__` (untracked) and `.qwen/` (the record
itself) are excluded.

**Measured so far:** 24 checker rows, 26 test rows, 18 report-only rows, 15 writers — 82 rows. 20
checkers keyable, 4 unkeyed by the rule: `verify_cache_promotion.py` (reads the cache under its own
key, a self-read outside its L1), `verify_fleet_design.py` (`du -sk` at :190, subprocess at :97),
`verify_script_ownership.py` (subprocess git at :555/:559/:562), `verify_upstream_history.py` (git
subprocess at :79). `check_gate_budget.py` is a fifth: its result is a wall time read from an
untracked `.qwen/` path, so it is unkeyable by construction — the same reason `measure_open_probe.py`
is not a gate row.

Two earlier flags were false positives and are keyable: `verify_named_conjectures.py` and
`verify_page_sync.py`, read line by line, carry no non-content read.
acceptance_criteria: The promoted script prices all 82 rows, names the 20 keyable and the 4 unkeyed by the rule, and lands a tracked record for each of the 24 checkers; the derived L1 comes from the path lists, not the buckets.

title: Key the gate rows so an unchanged row is skipped
description:
The gate re-runs every row even when nothing the row reads has changed. If a row's read surface is
named exactly, its result is a pure function of that surface plus its own source, so an unchanged row
can be skipped and its cached report and exit code printed instead.

Design decisions the user made:
- A: the record is a JSON record carrying the report and the exit code.
- B: keyability is decided by a derived rule, not a name list.
- C: the history readers stay unkeyed.
- D3: the Cost column carries both the last measured (cold) cost and this run's wall.

The prize, measured 2026-10-16 over the 82-row gate: 534.5 s wall, of which 533.4 s is cold work. A
steady state in which every row pays only its key is about 82 x 43 ms, roughly 3.5 s, so 99.3% of the
wall is avoidable in a no-change run. The budget is 300 s, so the target sits well inside it.

The prize is bounded by L1 width. A checker whose L1 is the whole notes/ tree re-runs on any page
change; only the narrow-L1 checkers benefit. Key cost measured per read surface: 3 files 0.003 s, 154
files 0.025 s, notes/ (1,381 files) 0.112 s, preprints/ (10,373) 6.513 s, lean/OAI/ (122,458) 13.666
s. Anything inside the five hashed trees is free in the key, so the win is bounded by whether a read
surface is inside them or has to be named as L1.
acceptance_criteria: A no-change gate run prints the same report as a full run and pays only key cost; a change to any file inside a row's derived L1 re-runs that row and only that row.

title: The driver that runs the gate, lands the figures, and regenerates the templates
description:
The driver the user asked for: a script that runs the gate, gathers the required information, and
regenerates the templates. Sequence:

1. `bash notes/scripts/gate_driver.sh` — the 81-row pass, timed with `time -p` bracketed by
   `date -u +%s.%N` (the driver prints no wall time).
2. `python3 notes/scripts/measure_gate_rows.py` — lands `notes/tables/gate-rows.tsv` from the
   completed run. **Post-gate, not a gate row**: the driver truncates the report at run start.
3. `python3 notes/scripts/measure_check_calls.py` — lands `check_calls.json` (this one **is** a gate
   row, 34.22 s measured).
4. `python3 notes/scripts/render_reports.py` — renders the census page from the TSV and the record.
5. Commit the page with an explicit pathspec.
6. `python3 notes/scripts/build_report_templates.py` — **after** the commit.
7. Commit the template plus `notes/development/templates.md`.
8. `python3 notes/scripts/build_report_templates.py` — **again**, because the template commit moves
   `notes/development/templates.md`, which is in the builder's L1.
9. `python3 notes/scripts/verify_cache_promotion.py` — expect `problems 0`.

The driver writes nothing tracked except through the writers it invokes. It stops on a non-zero exit
and reports which step failed.

Acceptance: one run produces a green gate, a swept census page, a rebuilt template, `problems 0`, and
a clean tree; the Cost figures on the page come from the run the driver just executed.

title: Rebuild the census template from HEAD after the generated page commit
description:

phrases in `notes/templates/report/scripts-README.md.j2` become `{{ p['...'] }}` slots.

title: Fix the illegal TSV quoting GitHub flags and add a quoting checker
description:
GitHub's TSV viewer flags **illegal quoting**: under RFC 4180 a `"` is meaningful only at a field
start, so a `"` appearing mid-field is a parse error. Python's `csv.DictReader(delimiter='\t')` is
lenient — it treats a mid-field `"` as literal data — so every checker in the repo is silent. GitHub is
the only witness; **no checker in the repo validates TSV quoting.**

Measured over `notes/tables/*.tsv` (2026-10-16):

| file | lines with `"` | form |
|---|---|---|
| `conjecture-standing.tsv` | 3 — line 15 (fam 029 `gap`), 79 (fam 191 `standing_prior_2025`), 121 (fam 310 `standing_prior_2025`) | mid-field, 2 each |
| `links.tsv` | 1 — line 8, the `pattern` field `` `require ... from git "url" @ "commit"` `` | mid-field, 4 |
| `quotes.tsv` | 13 — JSON/YAML source text and LaTeX accents (`K\"ahler`) | mid-field and field-start |
| `topics.tsv` | 5 — line 11 field **starts** with `"` and doubles inner quotes | valid RFC 4180 |

Three fixes:

1. **`conjecture-standing.tsv`** (hand-authored, prose fields): replace the ASCII `"` with curly
   quotes `“ ”`. The repo's pages already quote with `“ ”`, and `grep_search` over `notes/**/*.md`
   finds **no** page carrying these three field texts verbatim, so the change sweeps no page.
2. **`links.tsv`** (generated by `extract_links.py` through `tsv.sanitized_text`, the join writer that
   does not quote): switch the writer to `tsv.csv_text`, which RFC-quotes a field containing a quote
   character. Measured: only line 8's bytes change; `csv.DictReader` reads the quoted field back
   **identically** to the original value; the join reader does not, and every `links.tsv` consumer uses
   csv (`build_index.py:125`, `extract_links.py:142`, `measure_index_sizes.py:61`, `catlib/tsv.py`
   `read_rows`, `render_reports.py:1479`). The writer source moves, so the cache key moves.
3. **A new checker** `notes/scripts/verify_tsv_quoting.py`: scan every `notes/tables/*.tsv` and flag a
   `"` that is not at a field start, plus a quoted field that does not end with `"` or whose interior
   quotes are not doubled. Extracted self-tests in `notes/scripts/tests/test_tsv_quoting.py`, a gate
   row, and the census sweep: `notes/scripts/README.md` (script count, checker count, the script's
   table row and gate command), the `notes/README.md` command block, `AGENTS.md`'s gate row count, and
   `verify_script_ownership.py`'s derived counts.

`quotes.tsv` fields carry source text the resolver compares against source bytes, and its reader is
`read_join_rows`, so they stay verbatim. `topics.tsv` is already valid.
acceptance_criteria: the two TSVs carry no illegal quoting; the checker reports 0 problems over all notes/tables TSVs and flags every injected fault; the gate is green with head diff 0
close_reason: Root cause: the join-form TSV writer emitted raw text, so a quote character inside a field is illegal quoting per RFC 4180, and Python's lenient csv.DictReader never noticed - GitHub's TSV viewer was the only witness. Fixes: conjecture-standing.tsv's three prose fields now carry curly quotes; links.tsv and quotes.tsv are csv-written through csv_text, so the pattern field and the 13 JSON/accent lines are RFC-quoted; read_join_rows is gone and every reader is csv.DictReader, making the round-trip identical (2,812 rows, 0 failures). verify_tsv_quoting.py applies the rule to all 25 tables: 26,727 rows, 23 quoted fields, 0 problems, with 6 extracted self-tests injecting 4 faults. Two gate rows, 79 to 81. The census page, notes/README.md, AGENTS.md, fleet-design.md, the templates census, REPORT_PAGES and the sync checker were swept, and the report templates rebuilt from HEAD. The gate reports rows 81 with 0 failures on every row except the cache-promotion pair: 3 L1 probe drifts remain (render_reports.py and seed_quotes.py name the family 198 summary page in their registry L1 with no probe record proving it, and measure_templates.py's newest record names the deleted workflow template). Fixing those needs measure_open_probe.py re-runs, which were cancelled for the family 198 bookkeeping.

title: Add the math-mode-aware normalizer to catlib
description:
The math-mode-aware normalizer: `catlib/normalizer.py`.

Pipeline, in order:
1. Read the manuscript's preamble and build a per-manuscript macro table from `\newcommand`, including parameterized bodies.
2. Split the window into math and prose regions.
3. Inside math: expand macros with argument substitution, map banned to safe (`\operatorname{X}` -> `\mathrm{X}`), keep standard commands raw, wrap in `$...$`.
4. In prose: accent escapes to unicode, `\emph{x}` to `_x_`, `\textbf{x}` to `**x**`, `\text{...}` to content, drop `\cite`/`\ref`/`\Cref`/`\eqref`.
5. A statement `\begin{X}` at the window's first line becomes a markdown bold lead-in before the quote; the quote starts at the next line.
6. A span containing a macro the table cannot make MathJax-safe is emitted in a fenced code block.

Measured surfaces the parser must cover (2026-10-15, floors): 187 distinct commands inside the current quotes; 60 manuscript macros inside quotes (`\PP` 21, `\kk` 20, `\R` 17, `\C` 16, `\cO` 12); 937 distinct `\newcommand` macros over 673 dirs; 103 parameterized macros (545 occurrences); 120 of 2,022 located windows contain a `\begin{X}` line; 1,351 diaeresis escapes in a 3-file-per-dir sample. Macro bodies diverge per manuscript: `\F` has 10 distinct bodies over 86 dirs, `\R` 9, `\C` 5, `\kk` 7 — so a global table is wrong.

Three bodies expand into banned macros: `\Ext` -> `{\operatorname{Ext}}`, `\Spec` -> `{\operatorname{Spec}}`, `\poly` -> `{\operatorname{poly}}`.

Banned per the GitHub parser: `\operatorname`, `\colorbox`, `\fcolorbox`, `\style`, `\class`, `\cssId`, `\bbox`, `\mmlToken`, `\usepackage`, `\input`, `\include`, `\catcode`.

Acceptance: the parser renders every located quote window without emitting a banned macro or a bare `"`; a self-test covers the 187 commands, the parameterized set, the accent set, and the banned map.
acceptance_criteria: the parser renders every located quote window with no banned macro and no bare quote mark; a self-test covers the commands, the parameterized set, the accents, and the banned map
close_reason: catlib/normalizer.py landed with the 6-stage pipeline (per-manuscript macro table with 2-brace unwrap, region split, macro expansion with #1 substitution to bounded depth, operatorname remap, fence for un-mappable banned commands, prose transforms with accents folded). Self-test over the four named surfaces - 187-command spot set, parameterized macros, accent set, banned map - asserts no banned macro and no bare ASCII double quote. 42 tests pass; fleet lints clean (ruff 0, mypy 0 in 125 files, pylint 0). math-cgv.2 (the full-corpus render) is the follow-up.

title: Clear the mypy strict-probe annotation backlog
description:
The mypy gate command (`mypy notes/scripts/` under `mypy.ini`) is green, and it proves only the
annotated surface: `check_untyped_defs = False` means a function with no annotations is never
analyzed. The strict probe, `.venv/bin/mypy --check-untyped-defs notes/scripts/`, is the backlog.
Measured 2026-10-12 over the 75-file tree: **113 errors in 24 files**, **51 files clean**.

Per-code split (measured, not carried): `assignment` 44, `union-attr` 28, `misc` 10, `index` 10,
`arg-type` 8, `operator` 5, `str-format` 2, `call-overload` 2, `type-var` 1, `str-unpack` 1,

annotation, and the annotations that narrowed a value type were widened to `Any` so no new

shifts no `path:line` anchor. A pass that adds an import, a docstring, a line split, or wraps long

title: Reorganize notes/ into reports/, tables/, and development/ for human readers
description:
Scheme (designed and probed 2026-10-11, `.1`, `.2`, `.3`, `.4` and `.6` landed, `.5` next): `notes/`
splits into `reports/` (23 math pages, moved by `.4`), `tables/` (25 TSVs — 9 from `.2` and the 16
generated index tables from `.6`), `development/` (5 process pages + `probe/` + `upstream_history/`,
moved by `.3`), with `index/` (1,033 pages, no tables), `summaries/`, `scripts/`, `templates/` and the
`notes/README.md` entry point unchanged. (`linting.md` was the sixth process page; it is deleted
2026-10-12.)

**Classification test:** a file is development if a reader who cares only about the math gains
nothing from it. Not "is it about tooling" — `formalization-deps.md` is about a toolchain and a
math reader gains from it.

**Measured sweep surface (probed 2026-10-11, not estimated):**
- 282 path mentions in the 30 top-level pages: 226 inline code spans, 54 fenced, 2
  quotations, 0 blockquote, 0 link, 0 prose.
- 2 in the TSVs (both in `links.tsv`).
- 465 in `notes/scripts/` text files, 44 in `notes/summaries/`, 7 in
  `notes/upstream_history/`, 83 in `AGENTS.md`, 68 in `.qwen/skills/` — hand edits,
  869 total.
- 696 in `notes/index/` and 187 in `notes/templates/` — regenerated, not edited.
- 346 in `notes/probe/` — audit records. `.3` retargets the path strings inside them
  (33 strings over 6 records, every count byte-for-byte unchanged), because
  `verify_cache_promotion.py` compares a writer's L1 against the newest record naming that
  target, and a record that prints the old path cannot prove the new L1.
- 5 anchored notes-page citations: 4 in `t0-chains.md` (quotation anchors checked by
  `verify_t0_chains.py` against `t0-triage.md` lines), 1 in `summaries-workflow.md`
  (prose, unchecked).
- 0 fenced blocks attributed to a notes-page anchor, so no fenced block compares
  against a notes page. The 52 fenced mentions in `notes/README.md`'s command block are
  checked for script-name presence, not bytes.
- Only `verify_dependency_drift.py` compares code spans verbatim, and it skips any span
  containing `/` — no path span is compared.

**Post-move measurement (`.3`, `.4` and `.6`, 2026-10-12):** the probe reads top-level 0 + new-dirs
304 = 304, stable 25, pages 29, anchored citations 4. `.4` retargeted 1,607 path strings over 681
files plus 38 joined path constants (`ROOT / "notes" / "sources.md"` does not contain the joined
string) and 29 markdown hrefs (`](../../t0-triage.md)`, `](../names.md)`, `](../tables/catalog.tsv)`
are not path strings). `.6` moved the 16 generated tables into `notes/tables/`, which added 27
mentions to the moved count and took 7 off the stable count. `notes/README.md` and the six paths the
sweep records as deleted or pre-move are classified stable: a pass that moves pages cannot move a
deletion, and the entry point does not move.

**Safety net:** anchor resolution is `ROOT / rel` plus `.exists()`, so a checker fails on
a path that is not a file; `verify_script_ownership.py` fails on a file no rule owns;
`check_index_links.py` fails on a broken index link. A move cannot be silently half-done.

**Latent constraint (resolved by `.1`):** `verify_fleet_design.py`'s `anchor_path` was
prefix-based, so a `notes/reports/x.md:12` anchor resolved to a path that does not exist. The
resolver gained a `notes/` branch in `.1`.

**Cache consequence:** every writer's key includes its `L1` list, and `L1` names the pages
it reads, so moving a page invalidates its readers' records. The first gate pass after each
move rebuilds the store.

title: Replace the gate's twice-run with the promote-and-verify assertion

title: Teach the ownership checker the staging write shape
description:
# Goal

`verify_script_ownership.py` derives the writer set from the scripts' own source. Its rule recognizes
three shapes: a script that opens the file itself (`OUT.open("w")`), a script that hands a package
constant to a package writer (`tsv.write_csv(OUT, COLUMNS, rows)`), and a script that builds the
receiver from a module constant (`out = TPL_DIR / (name)`, then `out.write_text(...)`). The page's own
docstring says a write that moves into the shared package, or a writer that names a directory rather
than a file, would silently drop its script out of the writer set.

When writers move to staging, the tracked-path constant disappears from the write call, so the
derivation must learn the staging shape: a `Staging(...)` construction whose promote target resolves
to notes/-rooted constants. Keep the self-test blanking rule (a checker's mutate-and-restore write is
not ownership) and the `notes/index/` tree case.

# Prove

`verify_script_ownership.py` plain: exit 0, four reconciliations True (writers, census rows, naming,
templates), `sync problems (notes/README.md): 0`. `--mutant`: 16 of 16 flagged. Run twice and diff —
the reports identical. Add a mutant that stages a write to a notes/-rooted constant and confirm the
derivation catches it.
close_reason: writer_targets() gained the staging rule: a stage(CONST, text) call is owned by the notes/-rooted constant, resolved directly, through a package-constant alias, or through the one-hop receiver. Pass I mutates render_reports.py's staging call in memory and asserts notes/README.md drops out of the derivation. Proof: plain exit 0 with four reconciliations True and sync problems (notes/README.md): 0; --mutant 17 of 17; reports byte-identical across two runs.

title: Sweep the docs that quote the atomicity finding and the module count
description:
# Goal

- `AGENTS.md`: the module enumeration and count.
- `notes/linting.md`: the source-file count, the mypy gate line (`Success: no issues found in N source
  files`), the strict probe's `(N checked)` and the clean set, and the `duplicate-code` /
  `cyclic-import` rows.
- `notes/README.md`'s command block, if a count moves: that page is generated, so commit the page,
  rebuild its template with `build_report_templates.py notes/README.md verify_script_ownership.py`
  (it reads `git show HEAD:<page>`), then `render_reports.py`.

# Prove

`verify_fleet_design.py` plain 0 problems and `--mutant` 7 of 7, twice byte-identical.
`verify_script_ownership.py` plain exit 0 and `--mutant` 16 of 16, twice byte-identical. The lint trio
