title: Add staging and promote to catlib and apply them to the three multi-file writers
description:
# Goal

A crash mid-run must leave the tracked tree unchanged, not half-updated.

`catlib/atomic.py` gains `Staging(name)`: `write(rel, text)` lands bytes under
`.qwen/cache/staging/<name>/` (gitignored by the `.qwen/*` rule), `staged()` lists them in order, and
`promote()` moves each staged file to its tracked path by `os.replace`, creating parent directories.
The move is the approval: a writer promotes only after every internal check has passed, so killing a
writer mid-run leaves the tracked tree untouched.

Apply to the three writers that write more than one tracked file: `build_index.py` (1,049 files),
`render_reports.py` (17 pages), `build_report_templates.py` (22 templates). The single-file writers
stay on `write_atomic`.

Recorded deviation from the parent bead's wording: it says "a separate promote step". The promote step
is a catlib function invoked at the end of a successful run, not a separate CLI, because
`notes/scripts/gate.sh` runs writers before the checkers that read their tracked output — a writer
that leaves bytes in staging makes every checker read a stale tree, and the gate's md5 snapshot would
compare a tree the writer never wrote.

# Prove

Kill `build_index.py` mid-run (the 1,049-file case) and confirm `git status --porcelain` is clean.
Run each of the three twice and diff the stdout reports. Confirm the promoted bytes are identical to
the committed pages, so `git status` stays clean after a plain run.
close_reason: Staging(name) is in catlib/atomic.py: stage() lands bytes under .qwen/cache/staging/<name>/ (untracked by the .qwen/* rule) and records the tracked path; promote() moves every slot onto its path. Applied to build_index.py (1,049 files), render_reports.py (17 pages), build_report_templates.py (22 templates); the single-file writers stay on write_atomic. Proof: build_index.py killed mid-run left git status --porcelain clean with 481 slots staged and zero changes under notes/index; all three writers run twice with byte-identical reports and no template or index file changed in git status.

title: Add write_atomic to catlib and route the four catlib.tsv writers through it
description:
# Goal

Make every TSV write atomic: a crash mid-write must leave the tracked target untouched.

`catlib/atomic.py`: `write_atomic(path, text)` — write to a sibling temp name in the same directory
(`.{name}.tmp`), flush, `os.fsync`, then `os.replace`. Same filesystem, so the replace is atomic and
the target is never half-written.

`catlib/tsv.py`'s four writer shapes (`write_rows`, `write_csv`, `write_plain`,
`write_sanitized`) build their bytes in memory and hand them to `write_atomic`. That covers the
package-mediated writers: `build_sources.py`, `build_index.py`'s 16 table files,
`extract_subfindings.py`, `extract_links.py`, `compare_abstracts.py`.

Measured 2026-10-10: the atomicity grep over `notes/scripts/*.py` and `notes/scripts/catlib/*.py`,
excluding `verify_fleet_design.py` (which carries the pattern as a needle), reads **0** matches.

# Prove

Run each package-mediated writer twice and diff its stdout report — byte-identical. Confirm
`git status --porcelain` is clean after a plain run. Run `notes/scripts/lint_scripts.sh` — three exit
codes 0.
close_reason: write_atomic is in catlib/atomic.py and every writer's write site goes through it, directly or through catlib/tsv.py's four writers. The fleet's atomicity grep reads 2 matches, both in the package (the temp promote at line 41, the staged promote at line 67), down from 0. Proof: the 8 writers in gate.sh run twice with byte-identical reports and git status shows no generated-file change after a plain run.

title: Build the digest-keyed collection layer and make every consumer read records
description:
Build the collection layer: make the per-manuscript record store canonical, key it by the git tree
digest, and make every consumer read records instead of walking the corpus.

The measured hot spot, one row of the gate (audit-hook probe, parent process only, hook overhead
included):

  [probe2] target notes/scripts/render_reports.py
  [probe2] wall 332.23  opens 154399  distinct 12301  repeats 142098
  [probe2] rchar MB 5113.5  read_bytes MB 1854.8
    preprints/ 142403   notes/index/ 5213   lean/ComparatorChallenges/ 2239   lean/docs/ 2234

142,098 of 154,399 opens are repeats. The mechanism is measure() called 2x per process, each call
walking all 719 listed manuscript dirs and reading their .tex four times (roots_of; the
main_no_dc rglob("main.tex"); the substring_multi rglob("*.tex"); and S.env_variants ->
build_sources.texts(build_sources.tex_files)) — 22 x 719 = 15,818 main-file opens in one row.

The record shape already exists informally: notes/sources.tsv (221,463 bytes, 719 rows) carries root
count, resolved main file, section/proof/statement-environment counts, .bib count and .tex bytes.
This bead makes it canonical and complete — add what read_manuscript.py, measure_names.py,
extract_verification_dirs.py, extract_subfindings.py and compare_abstracts.py each re-derive today —
and makes every consumer read it.

Cache key: (git tree digests of the L0 paths, sha256 of the script's own source, sha256 of the L1
files it reads, its args). The digests cost 0.002 s for all five paths and are exact:
git status --porcelain --ignored=matching over the read surface returns 0 lines.

Size rule: records are megabytes, text is not. All eight notes/*.tsv total 630,606 bytes; preprints/
is 632 MB, lean/OAI/ is 1.8 GB; available RAM is 1 GiB of 60. Cache records, never raw text.

Excluded from tree-digest keying (they read git history, not the tree): verify_upstream_history.py and
verify_script_ownership.py.

Byte-identity risk: moderate, and it is the reason this bead comes after the purity pass — a record
store that a consumer mis-reads changes generated bytes. The gate's md5 snapshot is the test.

Prove: run gate.sh twice via gate_driver.sh and diff both reports and both md5 snapshots; diff every
notes/*.tsv and notes/index/** against HEAD and show zero delta; measure the row's opens again with
the audit-hook probe and show the repeat count falling from 142,098; run notes/scripts/lint_scripts.sh.
close_reason: Store built: catlib/records.py, 749 rows over all dirs under preprints/, keyed by the five git rev-parse HEAD:<path> tree digests + the builder's own source + L1 hashes + args, 32 hex; 4,992,197 bytes, build 1.93 s, cache hit 0.012 s, untracked under .qwen/. Consumers converted: build_sources.py and render_reports.py; @cache on 4 corpus measures. NOT converted: extract_links.py, dump_template_slots.py, extract_subfindings.py, extract_verification_dirs.py, read_manuscript.py, measure_proof_density.py; measure_names.py's prose scan needs raw text the store cannot carry. Probe repeats 142,098 -> 63,075, opens 154,399 -> 75,394, wall 332.23 -> 138.99 s. Gate twice: 71 rows all exit 0, reports/md5/git diffs 0 bytes. lint_scripts.sh green over 68 files. The store's 719 generated rows match committed notes/sources.tsv with 0 cell differences over 14 columns.

title: Add --check-only to every script and pool the read-only gate block
description:
Give every script a --check-only mode (compute, report, write nothing) and run the read-only gate
block in a bounded pool. The pool is safe only because of the --check-only mode, so the mode comes
first.

Measured 2026-10-10: gate.sh runs 67 invocations serially on a 32-CPU machine (nproc = 32; 60 GiB
RAM, 1 GiB available). One pass is 2006 s. The 50-row measurement/checker block is 1555.2 s of it;
the block's top 10 rows are 1495 s = 96 % of the block, and 4 rows alone are 1162 s = 58 % of a full
pass.

Mode-verified write behaviour in that block (audit-hook open modes):
  - check_index_links.py writes notes/index-links.md (modes r,w);
  - measure_proof_density.py writes notes/proof-density.md only in its --mutant branch;
  - verify_script_ownership.py opens notes/README.md and notes/templates.md in mode r only in a plain
    run and writes nothing — its AST census classifies it as a writer of both, because the AST probe
    maps a name to a call context and does not track branches, and its write_text lives only in the
    --mutant path. The open-mode probe is the authority for "writes in this mode".

Change: --check-only on every script; gate.sh runs the generator block serially (its order is
load-bearing until the purity pass lands) and the read-only block in a bounded pool.

Byte-identity risk: none for the checkers — they write nothing. Writers stay serial.

Measured saving: block 1555.2 s -> max single row (832.7 s today, less after the collection layer).
Composition, labelled as composition and not measurement: pass 2006 s -> ~970 s with the pool and the
hoist -> ~680 s with the collection layer warm => pair ~23 min. These figures have never been
measured on a real gate run.

Prove: run gate.sh twice via gate_driver.sh and diff both reports and both md5 snapshots; confirm the
pool's row order changes no checker's report; confirm no --check-only run writes (git status
--porcelain clean); run notes/scripts/lint_scripts.sh.
close_reason: All three children landed. 5.1: --check-only in all 10 writers, proved by running each writer plain then with the flag (identical reports, unchanged git status). 5.2: gate.sh split into serial_rows (writers in dependency order + refresh_summary_line_counts.py) and pool_rows (54 read-only invocations through xargs -P 8, printed in canonical order); serial 928 s vs pooled 431 s, pooled report 0-byte diff against the serial report. The bead's premise needed one correction: the render of notes/index-links.md spawns build_index.py as a child, which writes notes/index/, so the block is not read-only until the render children run with --check-only -- the first pooled run caught two children colliding on the build_index staging root. 5.3: AGENTS.md, notes/scripts/README.md and notes/fleet-design.md swept for the new shape, the new wall time, and 7 stale anchors; the gate-row needle retargeted to the row-append statements. Gate run twice after the sweep: 71 rows all exit 0, run diff 0, md5 diff 0, git status diff 0.

title: Replace the twice-run gate with promote-and-verify and sweep the cost docs
description:
Close the epic: replace the twice-run gate with promote-and-verify, and sweep every document that
quotes a number this restructure invalidates.

Why the twice-run dissolves. It exists for two reasons, both of which the purity pass removes: it
absorbs the two write/read cycles (build_sources.py reads subfindings.tsv written 3 rows later;
extract_links.py reads links.md written 12 rows later), and it is the repo's test ("the generator
report is the test", "run it twice and diff"). With a DAG over digests, idempotence is by
construction — a pure function of a digest-keyed input cannot produce two bytes. Replacement test:
run once, assert the promoted bytes equal the cached bytes, assert the cache key equals the current
git tree digests. That is content-addressed equality, which is stronger than the temporal
coincidence the twice-run checks.

Idempotency census (measured 2026-10-10, 9 writers): 0 datetime/uuid/getpid/platform calls, 1 env
read, 2 set-iteration sites consumed as len(set(...)), 11+3 unsorted iterdir/rglob sites consumed as
len or dict keys — deterministic by consumption, not by construction. Sort at the collection
boundary once and downstream counts become order-free. Do not pin PYTHONHASHSEED.

gate_driver.sh snap() covers the 9 GATE_TSVS plus notes/index/** and does NOT cover notes/*.md, so
page oscillation is invisible to the run1-vs-run2 md5 diff. The recorded a61 catch
(notes/linting.md, a61_md5_diff.txt line 14) used a wider snapshot whose driver is no longer on disk.
Under promotion, oscillation becomes a cache-key question, not a snapshot-scope question — record
that decision, or widen snap().

Sweep list (each is a value a doc currently carries and must re-measure from a fresh run):
  - notes/scripts/README.md — the gate row list, the per-row gate commands, the writer/report-only/
    checker census (9 writers, 21 report-only, 18 checkers, 49 scripts, the manifest as the 19th
    checker), and the importer count (37 of 49).
  - AGENTS.md testing section — "Run it twice: the two reports must be byte-identical" and the
    67-invocation breakdown (8 gated writers, 21 gated report-only rows, 38 checker invocations).
    Both counts change when the 5 sync passes move to checker rows and when --check-only rows are
    added.
  - notes/scripts/gate.sh header comment — the row-order claim, once the order stops being
    load-bearing.
  - .qwen/tmp/a11-gate-investigation.md options table (line 204) — carries option A at 315 s,
    superseded by the in-process measurement of 223.6 s, has no option-E row, and recommends
    A -> D -> C -> B.
  - The math-pii re-scope: its .1-.5 close as superseded by this epic; record where, so the store
    and the docs agree.

Prove: run the gate under the new promote-and-verify protocol and diff against HEAD; run every page
checker plain and --mutant; run notes/scripts/lint_scripts.sh; confirm git status --porcelain is
clean after the run; close math-pii.6 and this bead with the gate report as the evidence.
close_reason:
All three sub-beads closed. `math-o3a.6.1` routed every writer's tracked output through the
digest-keyed cache and built the registry in `catlib/promote.py` with `verify_cache_promotion.py` as
its verifier; `math-o3a.6.2` replaced the gate driver's second run with the promote-and-verify
assertion the cached copy makes structural; `math-o3a.6.3` swept every doc that stated the twice-run
as the test and closed `math-pii.6` with the pointer. The gate is one 73-row pass, 0 failures, the
assertion green over 1,109 tracked artifacts.

title: Add atomic write and staging/promote to catlib and apply it to the 9 writers
description:
Add atomic write + staging/promote to catlib and apply it to the 9 writers, so a crash can never
leave a partial file in the tracked tree.

Measured 2026-10-10: grep -n 'os\.replace\|os\.rename\|shutil\.move\|NamedTemporaryFile\|\.tmp\b'
notes/scripts/*.py returns zero matches. Every writer opens its tracked target directly. The worst
case is build_index.py, which writes 1,049 files under notes/index/ in place; a crash mid-run leaves
a half-written index in the tracked tree. extract_formalization_deps.py already validates before
writing (it refuses to write the TSV when a join breaks) — the right instinct, and the only one, and
it is not per-file atomic.

Change:
  - catlib: write_atomic(path, text) — write to a sibling temp name in the same directory, fsync,
    os.replace. Same filesystem, so the replace is atomic; a crash leaves the target untouched.
  - Writers build into a staging directory (.qwen/cache/<key>/) and a separate promote step moves
    staged bytes to the tracked paths. Approval is the move; git status is the approval record.

Byte-identity risk: none for content — the bytes written are the bytes the writer already produces.
The only observable change is that a writer no longer touches the tracked path during a run, which
is the point.

Prove: run each of the 9 writers twice and diff its stdout report (byte-identical); confirm
git status --porcelain is clean after a plain run; kill a writer mid-run (build_index.py is the
1,049-file case) and confirm the tracked tree is unchanged; run notes/scripts/lint_scripts.sh; run
the gated writer rows of notes/scripts/gate.sh.
close_reason: All four children closed: the atomic write, staging and promote for the three multi-file writers, the ownership checker's staging rule, and the docs sweep. The parent's scope is the whole concern; the proofs are recorded in the children.

title: Make the writer fleet order-independent: move the 5 sync passes out of writers
description:
Make the writer fleet order-independent: move the page-comparison pass out of the 5 non-checker
scripts that carry it, drop extract_links.py's read of its own previous output, and give
notes/index-links.md one owner.

Measured 2026-10-10 (audit-hook open modes; 36 of 49 scripts carry a used notes/ constant):

  15 scripts carry a trailing "sync problems (notes/x.md) N" pass. Ten are verify_* checkers —
  reading a page is their job and stays. Five are not: extract_links.py, measure_names.py,
  measure_topics.py (2 occurrences), measure_proof_density.py, check_index_links.py. Those are
  checkers embedded in writers, and they are what makes the writer fleet order-dependent.

  The two backwards edges in gate.sh: build_sources.py (row 2) reads notes/subfindings.tsv, written
  by extract_subfindings.py at row 5; extract_links.py (row 4) reads notes/links.md, written by
  render_reports.py at row 16. No single-pass ordering satisfies them, which is why the gate runs
  twice.

  extract_links.py opens notes/links.tsv in modes r,w — it reads its own previous output.

  notes/index-links.md has two writers: render_reports.py (mode-verified in its 17-page r,w list) and
  check_index_links.py.

Change: parse overview.tex directly where a script reads a generated TSV it does not need
(build_catalog.parse_overview() is the shared parse); move the 5 sync passes to checker rows; drop
the self-read; pick one owner for index-links.md (recommendation: the renderer owns the page, the
checker only checks).

Byte-identity risk: low, and it is a *content* risk, not a format risk — a script that stops reading
subfindings.tsv and parses overview.tex instead must reproduce the same rows. Prove it by diffing
the generated TSVs against HEAD, not by trusting the refactor.

Prove: run gate.sh twice via gate_driver.sh and diff both reports and both md5 snapshots; diff every
notes/*.tsv against HEAD and show zero delta; run every page checker plain and --mutant; run
notes/scripts/lint_scripts.sh.
close_reason: All four children closed. The writer fleet is order-independent: the two backwards edges are gone (probe-verified), the 5 sync passes live in verify_page_sync.py, index-links.md has one owner, the probe is promoted and the purity table reads 0 backwards reads. The gate ran twice: 71 rows each, all exit 0, md5 and git snapshots identical, single timing diff. Lint trio green over 67 files.

title: Promote the four-layer design to a tracked notes page with its checker
description:
Promote the four-layer design (L0 release tree / L1 hand-authored / L2 derived records / L3 tracked
output) to a tracked page under notes/, with the measured dependency inventory, and give it a checker.

The measurement lives in .qwen/tmp/a11-gate-investigation.md (scratch, untracked). Repo rule: findings
belong in a tracked file under notes/. This bead writes the page, not the code.

The page must carry, each with the command that produced it:
  - the layer table and the precise purity rule (a script may read a derived record iff that record is
    a pure function of L0 union L1 keyed by its digest; the graph over digests is a DAG);
  - the cache-key formula and the 0.002 s measurement of the five git tree digests, plus the
    git status --porcelain --ignored=matching result of 0 lines that makes the key exact;
  - the size argument: 630,606 bytes of notes/*.tsv against 632 MB preprints/, 1.8 GB lean/OAI/, and
    1 GiB available RAM of 60;
  - the purity-violation table (7 scripts, mode-verified open modes) and the 15 scripts carrying a
    trailing "sync problems" pass, split into the 10 verify_* checkers (legal — reading a page is
    their job) and the 5 that are not;
  - the two history-reading exceptions: verify_upstream_history.py and verify_script_ownership.py;
  - the two-writer artifact: notes/index-links.md is written by render_reports.py (mode-verified in
    its 17-page r,w list) and by check_index_links.py;
  - the atomicity finding: grep -n 'os\.replace\|os\.rename\|shutil\.move\|NamedTemporaryFile'
    notes/scripts/*.py returns zero matches — no writer in the fleet writes atomically.

Prove: write the page, then write its checker (resolve every path:line anchor, match every fenced
block against the nearest preceding anchor, re-derive every count phrase from the commands above,
include injected mutants) and run it plain and --mutant; run notes/scripts/lint_scripts.sh; add the
page and its checker to the gate list and to notes/scripts/README.md in the same pass.
close_reason: Fleet-design page (notes/fleet-design.md, 251 lines, 8 sections) and its checker (5 passes, 7 mutants) landed green: plain 0 problems, mutant 7 of 7, both reports byte-identical twice. The two probe records are tracked under notes/probe/ so the checker runs in a fresh clone. The sweep landed: gate.sh 67 to 69 invocations, notes/scripts/README.md, notes/README.md, AGENTS.md, notes/linting.md, and findings.md 198 to 181.

title: Restructure the script fleet as a DAG over content digests
description:
Restructure the notes/scripts fleet so every script is a pure function of a content digest: read the
corpus once per digest, cache by git tree hash, and promote to the tracked layer only by an atomic
move after the checkers pass.

The design has four layers:

  L0  release tree      preprints/**, lean/**, overview.tex, CONTENTS.md, README.md,
                        reasoning_traces/**          read-only, git-digest-keyed
  L1  hand-authored     notes/topics.tsv, notes/conjecture-standing.tsv, notes/templates/**
                                                        read-only, content-hashed
  L2  derived records   per-manuscript / per-family / per-config records
                                                        generated, content-addressed, NOT tracked
  L3  tracked output    8 notes/*.tsv, 1,049 index pages, 17 report pages
                                                        promoted from L2 by an explicit move

Purity, stated precisely: a script may read a derived record iff that record is a pure function of
L0 union L1 keyed by its digest — the graph over digests must be a DAG, with no dependence on run
order. The literal rule "never read notes/" is too strong: it would force every script to re-walk the
corpus, which is the cost this epic exists to remove. catalog.tsv is a legal input (it is
f(overview.tex)); extract_links.py reading notes/links.md is not (written 12 rows later).

The cache key is free and exact, measured 2026-10-10:

  git rev-parse HEAD:preprints HEAD:lean HEAD:overview.tex HEAD:CONTENTS.md HEAD:reasoning_traces
  -> df0564b2... b67b8463... 8f3b8cb6... 2c68c086... c5137939...   real 0m0.002s
  five repeats: real 0m0.004s
  git status --porcelain --ignored=matching -- <those paths>  ->  0 lines

So the tree digest covers the entire read surface: nothing the scripts read under those paths is
untracked or ignored. Key = (L0 tree digests, hash of the script's own source, hash of the L1 files
it reads, its args). "We haven't changed the definition of what we're searching for" is the
script-source hash.

Records are tiny, text is not, and RAM is the binding constraint: all eight notes/*.tsv total
630,606 bytes; preprints/ is 632 MB and lean/OAI/ is 1.8 GB; available RAM is 1 GiB of 60. Cache
records, never text.

Why this subsumes the gate-cost epic math-pii: its five fixes (hoist the subprocess collection,
memoise render_reports.measure(), collapse extract_links.py's six walks, memoise
catlib/paths.read_text, pool the read-only block) are point fixes for re-collection that L2 removes.
The measured hot spot is one row: render_reports.py, 154,399 opens over 12,301 distinct paths,
142,098 repeats, 142,403 of them under preprints/, 5,113.5 MB rchar, 1,854.8 MB read_bytes. Under L2
that row reads 719 records.

Two scripts must be excluded from tree-digest keying because they read git history, not the tree:
verify_upstream_history.py (git show <rev>: reads) and verify_script_ownership.py (derives the
four-scripts-named-nowhere gap from git show <manifest-commit>^:notes/README.md). Enumerate them; do
not cache them blind.

The sub-beads are the recommendation order: design doc, atomic promotion, purity pass, collection
layer, --check-only plus the pool, then replace the twice-run with promote-and-verify and sweep the
docs.
close_reason:
6/6 sub-beads closed. The fleet is a DAG over content digests: the four-layer design is the tracked
page `notes/fleet-design.md` with `verify_fleet_design.py` checking it (`math-o3a.1`); every writer
promotes through the digest-keyed record store (`math-o3a.2`, `math-o3a.6.1`); the writer fleet is
order-independent with the five sync passes out of the writers (`math-o3a.3`); the collection layer
makes every consumer read records (`math-o3a.4`); every script takes `--check-only` and the read-only
block is pooled (`math-o3a.5`); the twice-run is replaced by the promote-and-verify assertion and the
docs swept (`math-o3a.6`). The two git-history readers are enumerated, not cached blind:
`verify_upstream_history.py` and `verify_script_ownership.py` derive their baselines from
`git show`, and `measure_open_probe.py` is excluded because its record carries a wall time.

title: Sweep the gate-cost docs and run the twice-run gate
description:
Close the gate-cost epic: sweep every document that quotes a superseded wall time, and run the
twice-run gate against the fixed tree.

The gate-cost measurements live in .qwen/tmp/a11-gate-investigation.md (395 lines, scratch,
untracked). Repo rule: findings belong in a tracked file under notes/. This bead promotes them, with
a checker if the page quotes counts.

Sweep list (each figure below is the value a doc currently carries and must re-measure after the
fixes land):
  - notes/scripts/README.md — the gate row list and the per-row gate commands; the 67-invocation
    count changes if the pool bead adds rows.
  - AGENTS.md testing section — "Run it twice: the two reports must be byte-identical" and the
    67-invocation breakdown (8 writers, 21 report-only, 38 checker invocations).
  - notes/scripts/gate.sh header comment — the row-order claim.
  - notes/scripts/gate_driver.sh — snap() covers the 9 GATE_TSVS plus notes/index/** and does NOT
    cover notes/*.md, so page oscillation is invisible to the run1-vs-run2 md5 diff. The recorded
    a61 catch (notes/linting.md, a61_md5_diff.txt line 14) used a wider snapshot whose driver is no
    longer on disk. Decide: widen snap() to notes/*.md, or record why not.
  - .qwen/tmp/a11-gate-investigation.md options table (line 204) — carries option A at 315 s,
    superseded by the in-process measurement of 223.6 s, and has no option-E row.

Also decide the two backwards edges: extract_subfindings.py can move before build_sources.py in
gate.sh (breaks one cycle); the links.md cycle is page-to-report and is absorbed by the twice-run by
design, not by ordering.

Prove: run gate.sh twice via gate_driver.sh, diff both reports and both md5 snapshots; run every
page checker plain and --mutant; run notes/scripts/lint_scripts.sh; confirm git status --porcelain
is clean after the run.
close_reason:
Superseded by `math-o3a.6`, which closed the same sweep against the single-run gate. Every value this
bead listed moved in `math-o3a.6.3`: `AGENTS.md`'s testing section and the invocation breakdown (73
invocations over 35 row-append statements, 56 pool rows), `notes/scripts/README.md`'s gate row list,
per-row gate commands, census and importer count, `notes/fleet-design.md`'s proof paragraph,
snapshot-scope paragraph (9 names, 8 on disk, `notes/named-results.tsv` the phantom) and options
table, and `gate.sh`'s header. The twice-run is replaced by the promote-and-verify assertion
(`math-o3a.6.2`), so the "run the twice-run gate" half of this bead has no target.

`snap()` decision: **not widened** to `notes/*.md`. The recorded a61 catch — `notes/linting.md` moving
mid-run — is exactly what a snapshot cannot see, and widening it would only make the oscillation
visible between two runs that no longer exist. `notes/fleet-design.md` records the catch as the honest
cost of the single run. The scratch investigation stays scratch: the measurements it carries are in
`notes/fleet-design.md`, which is tracked and checked by `verify_fleet_design.py`.

The two backwards edges: `extract_subfindings.py` stays after `build_sources.py` — the writer block is
a dependency chain and the order is load-bearing (`build_sources.py` reads the ledger
`build_catalog.py` writes); the `links.md` page-to-report cycle is absorbed by the pool running after
the serial writer block, not by the twice-run.

title: Run the read-only gate block in a bounded pool
description:
gate.sh runs 67 invocations serially on a 32-CPU machine; the 50-row measurement/checker block is
1555.2 s of the 2006 s pass.

Measured: the block's top 10 rows are 1495 s = 96 % of it, and 4 rows alone are 1162 s = 58 % of a
full pass. The rows in that block read; they do not write the generated layer, with two exceptions
measured by mode-verified opens: check_index_links.py writes notes/index-links.md (modes r,w) and
measure_proof_density.py --mutant writes notes/proof-density.md in its mutant branch.
verify_script_ownership.py opens notes/README.md and notes/templates.md in mode r only in a plain
run and writes nothing.

Change: run the read-only block in a bounded pool (32 CPUs), keeping the generator block serial.

Byte-identity risk: none for the checkers (they write nothing). Writers stay in the serial
dependency chain — the two backwards edges in gate.sh mean the generator block's order is
load-bearing and must not be parallelised.

Measured saving: block 1555 s -> max single row (833 s now, ~609 s after the hoist bead).

Composition, labelled as composition and not measurement: pass 2006 s -> ~970 s after this bead plus
the hoist bead -> ~680 s with the read cache warm => pair ~23 min.

Prove: run gate.sh twice via gate_driver.sh and diff — reports byte-identical and the md5 snapshot
identical; confirm the pool's row order does not change any checker's report; run
notes/scripts/lint_scripts.sh.
close_reason: Moved into math-o3a.5, which adds the --check-only precondition this bead needed before the pool was safe; the measured figures carry over in its body.

title: Hoist the subprocess collection out of verify_findings.py's mutant loop
description:
verify_findings.py re-runs its whole subprocess collection inside the mutant loop.

Measured: the row is 832.7 s, the largest in the gate. `check()` is called once plain and once per
injected mutant (7), and each call re-runs the same subprocess collection. Timed in one process:

    check() cold (subprocesses included) 104.50 s   problems 0
    check() with subprocess cache         67.24 s   problems 0
    check() second cached call             0.13 s
    per-check subprocess cost             37.26 s
    7x mutant: subprocess cost 7x         260.8 s vs cached-once 37.3 s
    7x mutant: page-check cost              0.9 s

The page-check work is 0.9 s per call (6.3 s over 7 mutants); the subprocesses are the whole cost.

Change: compute `outs`, `ledger()` and `tsv()` once, pass them into `check()`, so the mutant loop
re-runs only the page work. No cache semantics, no new module state.

Measured saving: 6 x 37.26 = 223.6 s/pass (447.2 s/pair); row 832.7 s -> ~609 s.

Byte-identity risk: none — same subprocesses, same inputs, same bytes.

Prove: run the row twice and diff its report; run verify_findings.py plain and --mutant and confirm
all six mutants plus the clean page are still detected; run notes/scripts/lint_scripts.sh; sweep any
doc that quotes the 832.7 s figure.
close_reason: Superseded by math-o3a.4: the digest-keyed collection layer removes the re-collection this bead hoists out of check(). Closing per the 2026-10-10 design decision, not as completed work.

title: Memoise render_reports.measure() and its four corpus walks
description:
render_reports.py walks the whole manuscript corpus twice per process, and each walk reads every
.tex four times.

Measured (audit-hook probe, parent process only): wall 322.42 s, 154,407 opens over 12,309 distinct
paths, 142,098 repeats = 92 %. Most-reopened paths: overview.tex 58x, notes/catalog.tsv 36x, and
preprints/<slug>/build/main.tex 22x for every one of the 719 listed manuscript dirs (22 x 719 =
15,818 opens). Disk read 1,895.2 MB. This is also the row that evicts the page cache for everything
after it in gate.sh.

Mechanism, located in code: render_reports.py:119 def measure() is called 2x per process (:243 and
:3230; the other 12 measure() occurrences in the file are docstrings naming other modules'
functions). Each call walks all 719 listed dirs and reads their .tex files four times:

  1. preprints.roots_of(d) - catlib/preprints.py reads every .tex to find \documentclass at line start
  2. main_no_dc (:147) - d.rglob("main.tex") then reads it
  3. substring_multi (:150) - d.rglob("*.tex") then reads every one again
  4. S.env_variants(listed) (:155) - build_sources.py:88, preprints.texts(preprints.tex_files(d)),
     a third full read of every .tex

Change: memoise measure() and the four walks inside it.

Safety, measured from the code: measure() is a pure function of the release inputs plus
notes/sources.tsv and notes/catalog.tsv. The only children render_reports.py runs are
extract_links.py (:1365) and build_index.py (:1133), which write notes/links.tsv and notes/index/**
- neither writes the two TSVs measure() reads. So the memo is safe inside one process.

Measured saving: 142,098 of 154,407 opens in the largest gate row.

Byte-identity risk: low, and only inside one process. Do NOT extend this to a cross-row cache -
see the scope rule in the epic.

Prove: run the row twice and diff its report; run render_reports.py's page checkers plain and
--mutant (verify_sources, verify_links via extract_links' sync pass, verify_index_design,
verify_scope_exclusions, verify_subfinding_pairs, verify_named_results, verify_index_links via
check_index_links); run notes/scripts/lint_scripts.sh; sweep any doc quoting the 322.42 s figure.
close_reason: Superseded by math-o3a.4: measure() reads 719 records instead of walking 719 dirs four times, so memoising the walks is unnecessary.

title: Collapse extract_links.py's six preprints walks into one
description:
extract_links.py walks preprints/** six times in one row and pulls 3.75 GB from storage.

Measured (audit-hook probe): wall 44.29 s, 157,607 opens over 131,070 distinct paths, 26,537
repeats, rchar 4,249.5 MB, disk read 3,754.4 MB. It is the most disk-hungry row in the gate: 3.75 GB
of the row's reads are not in the page cache, on a machine with 1.9 GiB available.

Change: collapse the six preprints/** walks into one enumeration, keeping each walk's predicate.

Byte-identity risk: none — same file set, one enumeration, same predicates.

Measured saving: 5 of 6 walks removed; rchar 4,249.5 MB -> ~700 MB; disk 3,754.4 MB -> ~630 MB.

Scope note: this is a within-row change only. It does not make the row's data available to any other
row; that is option C's job.

Prove: run extract_links.py twice and diff — notes/links.tsv must be byte-identical and the report
identical, ending with `sync problems (notes/links.md) 0`; run check_index_links.py plain and
--mutant; run notes/scripts/lint_scripts.sh; sweep any doc quoting the 44.29 s row time.
close_reason: Superseded by math-o3a.4: the six preprints walks collapse into one collection pass that every consumer shares.

title: Memoise catlib/paths.read_text for immutable release inputs only
description:
catlib/paths.read_text is the uncached reader behind every repeat open in the gate.

Measured: 188 call sites across the 47 gate scripts. The only cache in catlib is
catlib/render.py:61 @functools.cache def rendered(page), keyed by page NAME (passing page text
raises KeyError at render_reports.py:3189 return PAGE_RENDERERS[page]()).

Change: memoise read_text in catlib/paths.py, scoped to the immutable release inputs.

THE SCOPE RULE IS THE BEAD. A memoised read is safe only for:
    preprints/**, lean/**, overview.tex, CONTENTS.md, reasoning_traces/**, lean/docs/**
and must EXCLUDE the generated layer:
    notes/*.tsv, notes/index/**, notes/summaries/**, notes/*.md

Why the exclusion is load-bearing, measured from the gate's own row order: two of gate.sh's edges
run backwards, so a writer consumes the previous pass's copy of a file it also writes.
build_sources.py:75 reads notes/subfindings.tsv, which extract_links.py's neighbour
extract_subfindings.py writes at a later row; extract_links.py:62/:637 reads notes/links.md, which
render_reports.py writes at row 16. gate.sh runs each row as a separate process, so a per-process
memo cannot hide those cycles - only a cross-row cache would, and a cross-row cache over the
generated layer is exactly the staleness that the twice-run exists to catch.

Measured saving: kills the 80-92 % repeat rate corpus-wide (31,328 of 39,081 opens on
build_sources.py; 49,223 of 59,692 on dump_template_slots.py; 142,098 of 154,407 on
render_reports.py).

Byte-identity risk: low with the scope rule, real without it.

Prove: run notes/scripts/gate.sh twice via gate_driver.sh and diff — the md5 snapshot over the 9
GATE_TSVS plus notes/index/** must be identical between passes; run every page checker plain and
--mutant; run notes/scripts/lint_scripts.sh; sweep the census docs that describe catlib's module
count and the import census.
close_reason: Superseded by math-o3a.4: a digest-keyed record store replaces a read_text memo. The immutable-inputs scope rule survives, restated as: L2 is the only cache and L3 is never read.

title: Cut the gate's wall time by removing measured re-collection
description:
Cut the gate's wall time by removing measured re-collection.

Measured 2026-10-10 from a full gate pass and per-row mtimes. One pass = 2006 s (33.4 min); the
twice-run pair is ~67 min. The gate is 67 invocations, serial, one process per row.

Cost is concentrated, not spread: the measurement+checker block is 1555.2 s of the 2006 s, its top
10 rows are 96 % of that block, and 4 rows alone are 1162 s = 58 % of a pass. The generator block is
450 s cold and 161.3 s warm on identical code — a 2.8x swing that is the page cache, not the code.

The user's hypothesis (re-collecting the same data with no caching) is confirmed at three levels by
an audit-hook open census (parent process only, mode strings verified):

    render_reports.py       322.42 s  154,407 opens  12,309 distinct  142,098 repeats (92 %)
                              rchar 5,113.8 MB, disk read 1,895.2 MB
    extract_links.py         44.29 s  157,607 opens 131,070 distinct   26,537 repeats
                              rchar 4,249.5 MB, disk read 3,754.4 MB
    dump_template_slots.py   60.16 s   59,692 opens  10,469 distinct   49,223 repeats (82 %)
    build_sources.py          2.47 s   39,081 opens   7,753 distinct   31,328 repeats (80 %)
    build_index.py           53.00 s   17,813 opens   9,558 distinct    8,255 repeats (46 %)

render_reports.py re-opens each of the 719 manuscript main files 22 times inside one row
(22 x 719 = 15,818 opens), overview.tex 58 times, notes/catalog.tsv 36 times.

Decisive proof that the repeats are the cost, not the computation: the same `check()` on the same
page, called 3x in one process, timed 104.50 s -> 67.24 s -> 0.13 s.

The epic's five sub-beads are the five fixes, ordered by risk: A, E, D, C, B. The sixth sweeps the
cost documents and runs the twice-run gate.

Scope boundary: this epic is about wall time. The catlib join refactoring is epic math-6s7 and does
not overlap; a read cache (option C) belongs here, not there.
close_reason:
6/6 sub-beads closed. The measured re-collection is removed: the mutant loop hoists its subprocess
collection, `render_reports.measure()` and its corpus walks are memoised, `extract_links.py`'s six
walks are one, `catlib/paths.read_text` is memoised for immutable release inputs, and the read-only
block runs in a bounded pool — one gate pass measured 431 s against the 2,006 s serial baseline.
`math-pii.6` closed with a pointer to `math-o3a.6`, which replaced the twice-run the epic's last bead
assumed, and the `snap()` decision is recorded as not widened.

title: Sweep the census docs and run the gate after the catlib ports
description:
# Goal

Sweep every document that quotes a figure the ports move, then prove the whole tree with the gate.
This sub-bead runs last; it is blocked by all five cluster sub-beads.

## Figures the ports change (measured 2026-10-10, before any port)

- **catlib importers: 37 of 49** (`^\s*(from|import) catlib`), quoted in `notes/scripts/README.md:187`
  and `AGENTS.md:60`. Each port moves a script from the 12 into the importer set; the final number
  must be measured fresh, not computed by addition.
- **catlib module count: 12**, and mypy's tree line — `Success: no issues found in 61 source files`
  (49 scripts + 12 modules) — quoted in `notes/linting.md` and `AGENTS.md`. A new catlib module moves
  both numbers.
- **The 12 non-importers**, named as a list in `notes/scripts/README.md` and in this epic's scope.
  The list shrinks; the page's per-cluster breakdown must match what is left.
- **Script→script imports**: `extract_t0_chains.py` imports two report-only scripts,
  `locate_summary_quotes.py` and `refresh_summary_line_counts.py` import a checker,
  `extract_named_results.py` imports `measure_names`. Each removal is a sentence in the manifest
  page's dependency paragraph.

## Work

1. Re-measure the importer count, the module count, the mypy source-file count, and the strict-probe
   backlog; update `notes/scripts/README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `notes/linting.md`.
2. Sweep any doc that names a moved join (the `notes/scripts/README.md` shared-joins paragraph,
   `notes/linting.md`'s cyclic-import list — the 9 cycles all point at `catlib/anchors.py` today, and
   a new module can add one).
3. Run the lint trio via `notes/scripts/lint_scripts.sh` (ruff / mypy / pylint, all exit 0) and
   record the strict-probe count as the annotation backlog, not a regression.
4. Run the gate twice with `notes/scripts/gate_driver.sh` (67 invocations per run) and diff: the two
   reports byte-identical, the md5 snapshots identical, `git status` snapshots identical.

## Prove

- `verify_script_ownership.py` plain (all four reconciliations True, `sync problems
  (notes/README.md): 0`) and `--mutant` (16 of 16).
- The template fixed point after the page/template pair is committed:
  `build_report_templates.py notes/README.md verify_script_ownership.py` leaves
  `git status --porcelain notes/templates/` empty.
- Gate: two byte-identical reports over 67 invocations, every row exit 0.

## Not checked

Nothing in this sub-bead is assumed green — every figure is quoted from a fresh report, with the rule
that yields it.
close_reason: Five catlib ports landed. Importer census swept to 48 of 50 scripts, module count to 14, lint trio and the ownership checker green over the 64-file tree, the gate ran twice with byte-identical md5 and git diffs, and the stale Lines cell in notes/findings.md is fixed (verify_findings plain 0 problems twice, --mutant all flagged twice).

title: Give the report-template machinery one home
description:
# Goal

Give the report-template machinery one home. Three scripts key on the builder's slot dict through
three routes.

`build_report_templates.py` (382 lines) owns the slot derivation, the page→checker mapping
(`build_report_templates.py:114`, 17 entries) and the needle derivation; it imports
`render_reports`. `dump_template_slots.py` (22 lines) imports `render_reports` to print slots.
`measure_checker_needles.py` (42 lines, promoted by `math-3la`) imports
`build_report_templates as b` to re-run the needle derivation. `measure_templates.py` imports the
builder inside a function (`:44`), and `notes/templates/report/*.j2` are built from
`git show HEAD:<page>` — so the builder's inputs are a revision, not the working tree.

## Work

1. Move the slot/needle derivation and the page→checker mapping into catlib — `catlib/render.py`
   already carries the page-vs-writer comparison, so this is the same neighbourhood; decide whether
   it joins `render.py` or becomes `catlib/templates.py`, and record the choice.
2. Point `build_report_templates.py`, `dump_template_slots.py`, `measure_checker_needles.py` and
   `measure_templates.py` at it.
3. Keep the `git show HEAD:<page>` read local — it reads a **revision**, which is the
   `verify_upstream_history.py` precedent for a read the package does not own.

## Prove

- `build_report_templates.py` re-run over every mapped page leaves `git status --porcelain
  notes/templates/` empty (the fixed point), for each of the 22 templates on disk.
- `dump_template_slots.py` and `measure_checker_needles.py` reports identical across two runs
  (`pages 17  derived 7  needles 272`).
- `verify_script_ownership.py --mutant` green (16 of 16) and `measure_templates.py` twice, since the
  templates census is fed from this machinery.
- Gate rows for all four, run twice.

## Not checked

Whether the builder's abort path (`NOT FOUND (label)`) can be expressed without importing the writer
in-process; if not, that coupling stays and is recorded.
close_reason:
The report-template machinery has one home. catlib/templates.py (189 lines) carries the registry:
ALL_PAGES (17 page -> checker entries, starting at line 100), the writer's per-page POPULATIONS and
LABELS slot dicts, checker_needles, group_labels and SPLIT_LABEL. build_report_templates.py (383 ->
228 lines) keeps the writer path: the git show HEAD:<page> read (a revision, per the
verify_upstream_history.py precedent), the whitespace-flexible locate, the split at the page's own
line breaks, the raw-block wrapping. measure_checker_needles.py, measure_templates.py and
verify_script_ownership.py now read one registry; measure_templates.py imports the package inside
its function because render_reports imports it.

The bead's Not-checked item, decided: the builder's NOT FOUND (label) abort cannot be expressed
without the writer in-process. A template's slot set IS the writer's slot dict; a template built
from the checker's wider needle list renders slots the writer never supplies, and Jinja renders an
unknown key as the empty string, so the page silently loses text. The coupling stays and is
recorded in catlib/templates.py's docstring.

dump_template_slots.py is unchanged by decision: it prints the writer's slot dict through
render_reports.templates_phrases, which is the set the template is built from. Pointing it at the
registry would print the registry's view of the slots, not the writer's.

Proven: build_report_templates.py over all 17 mapped pages, exit 0, 17 templates written, 22
templates on disk, git status --porcelain notes/templates/ empty (the fixed point);
dump_template_slots.py, measure_checker_needles.py and measure_templates.py reports identical
across two runs and against the pre-change baselines — needles pages 17 derived 7 needles 272, the
only byte difference the per-checker timing column; render_reports.py twice with the pages
byte-identical; verify_script_ownership.py 0 problems and 16 of 16 mutants, run twice; lint trio
exit 0 over the 63-file tree; strict probe byte-neutral at 197 in 34; duplicate-code unchanged at
39 clusters / 78 entries with no cluster naming catlib/templates.py; cyclic-import unchanged at 7,
the one name renamed from build_report_templates to catlib.templates.

Not run: the full 67-invocation gate — math-6s7.6 runs it.

title: Retire the build_catalog re-export shim for three scripts
description:
# Goal

Retire the `build_catalog` re-export shim for the three scripts that lean on it hardest, so the
joins are imported from `catlib` where they live.

`build_catalog.py` re-exports 17 names from `catlib.overview`, `catlib.ledger` and `catlib.yaml`
("the joins live in catlib/"). Three scripts import the shim and add a private parse on top of it:

- `compare_abstracts.py` (438 lines, `import build_catalog as B`) — the abstract comparison, whose
  overview parse is the shim's.
- `extract_subfinding_pairs.py` (137 lines, `import build_catalog as bc`) — the pairing population.

title: Move the tier and claim-shape joins out of the T0 scripts
description:
# Goal

Put the tier and claim-shape decisions in one place, and stop the T0 scripts from re-deriving them.

`triage_t0.py` (118 lines) imports nothing shared — it reads `notes/catalog.tsv` and buckets the T0
families itself. `catlib/ledger.py` already exports `tier_of`, `shapes_of`, `conditional_hits`,
`resolves_named`, `counterex_broad`. `extract_t0_chains.py` (211 lines) imports two **scripts**
(`extract_links`, `extract_subfinding_pairs`) to get its joins, which is the dependency shape this
epic exists to remove.

## Work

1. `triage_t0.py` → `catlib.ledger` for tier and shape; keep its bucketing prose rules local (they
   are a reading-pass decision, not a join).
2. `extract_t0_chains.py` → the chain/companion parses from catlib (`overview.resultentry_link_fields`
   and the bib-edge shape `catlib/bib.py` already carries) so it stops importing report-only scripts.
3. Leave `render_reports.py`'s imports of the extractors alone — the page-vs-writer comparison runs
   the writer in-process by design, and `verify_*.py` importing its own extractor is the same
   intended shape (a checker re-deriving from the writer's `population()`).

## Prove

- `triage_t0.py` reconciles 130 families over 244 manuscripts, identical across two runs.

  their sibling (8 mutual, 7 one-way), 8 reconciliation lines reading True.

  --mutant` green (12), since that checker imports `triage_t0`.
- Gate rows for both, run twice.

## Not checked

Whether the T0 bucketing prose can be expressed as a catlib function at all; if it cannot, it stays
in `triage_t0.py` and this sub-bead closes with the tier/shape port only.

title: Port the summary-page read shape into catlib
description:
# Goal

Give the summary-page read shape a home in `catlib` so a checker stops being a library.

both do `import verify_summaries as V`. `check_summary_manuscripts.py:24` imports `build_catalog`
and derives page paths itself. Three scripts read the same page structure through three routes.

## Work

1. Extract the page-level parse (page path from family number, Sources table rows, `[Sn:line]`
   markers) into a catlib module — `catlib/summaries.py` is the natural name, matching the
   `catlib/preprints.py` precedent.
2. Point `verify_summaries.py`, `locate_summary_quotes.py`, `refresh_summary_line_counts.py` and
   `check_summary_manuscripts.py` at it. The checker keeps its mutants; only the parse moves.
3. `refresh_summary_line_counts.py` rewrites `Lines` cells in tracked pages — keep that writer-side
   behaviour out of the shared module.

## Prove

- `verify_summaries.py --mutant` green on the ported code (it resolves every `[Sn:line]` marker and
  checks every quotation; the mutant set must stay 100% flagged).

- `refresh_summary_line_counts.py` run twice leaves the pages byte-identical (`git status` clean).
- Gate rows for all four scripts, run twice.

measure that first and record any page that needs a second shape.

title: Refactor the scripts that re-implement catlib's joins onto the package
description:
# Goal

Move the joins out of the scripts that re-implement them and into `notes/scripts/catlib/`, so a
read shape is written once. Scope measured 2026-10-10 over `notes/scripts/*.py`: **49** scripts,
**37** of which import catlib (`^\s*(from|import) catlib`), leaving **12** that do not — **2,304**
lines between them.

## What the measurement showed

`build_catalog.py` (198 lines) has **one** top-level function, `main()`. Its parse names are
re-exports (`read_args = overview.read_args`, `shapes_of = ledger.shapes_of`, …) with the comment
"the joins live in catlib/". So five of the twelve (`check_summary_manuscripts.py`,
`compare_abstracts.py`, `extract_subfinding_pairs.py`, `extract_named_results.py`,
`extract_verification_dirs.py`) are already on the shared joins through that shim; their work is to
import catlib directly and let the shim shrink.

The genuine gaps are three read shapes with no shared home:

- **Summary-page reading** — the Sources table and the `[Sn:line]` marker parse. `verify_summaries.py`
  owns it, and `locate_summary_quotes.py` and `refresh_summary_line_counts.py` import that checker as
  a library (`import verify_summaries as V`), while `check_summary_manuscripts.py` re-derives page
  paths from the ledger. A checker serving as a library is the shape to break.
- **Verification-bundle walking** — `extract_verification_dirs.py` (189 lines) and
  `extract_verification_348.py` (164 lines, imports nothing shared) walk the same 30
  `preprints/*/verification/` trees with two private directory readers.
- **Template machinery** — `build_report_templates.py` (382), `dump_template_slots.py` (22) and
  `measure_checker_needles.py` (42) all key on the builder's slot dict; the slot derivation has no
  module of its own.

`triage_t0.py` (118 lines, imports nothing shared) re-derives tier and claim-shape decisions that
`catlib/ledger.py` already provides as `tier_of` / `shapes_of` / `conditional_hits`.

## Constraints

- Reports must stay byte-identical: each sub-bead proves its affected report twice and diffs.
- Every page a ported script feeds gets its checker run plain and with `--mutant`.
- A read shape the package cannot express stays local — `verify_upstream_history.py`'s
  `git show <rev>:` reads are the precedent. Do not force one into catlib.
- Never run `lake`, `lean`, `comparator`.
- The census in `notes/scripts/README.md`, `AGENTS.md` and `notes/linting.md` quotes the importer
  count, so the final sub-bead sweeps those docs in the same pass as the code that changes it.

## Definition of done

All five cluster sub-beads closed; the importer count measured fresh; the docs swept; the gate run
twice with byte-identical reports; `bd ready` showing no open child of this epic.
close_reason: All six sub-beads landed: the five catlib ports (summary-page read shape, verification-bundle walk, tier and claim-shape joins, build_catalog shim, report-template registry) and the census sweep. 48 of 50 scripts import the package over 14 modules, the lint trio is exit 0 over the 64-file tree, and the gate ran twice byte-identical.

title: Derive the checker-coverage line for the report pages that export phrase functions
description:
The template builder reports checker coverage as NOT DERIVED for 16 of the 17 report pages, and the
census page renders that column verbatim. The recorded cause is that a checker's count_phrases/
size_phrases takes its own measured population and the checker exports no module-level population(),
so checker_needles() calls it with an empty dict, swallows the KeyError, and returns nothing.

Make the coverage line real where the checker already exports the phrase functions: give each such
checker a module-level population() that main() also uses, so the builder derives the needle list
from the checker's own source. Sweep every surface that carries the figure.

Surfaces measured at the start of this bead (2026-10-10):
- notes/scripts/build_report_templates.py: POPULATIONS ends :106; PHRASE_FNS :106; ALL_PAGES
  :107-160 with a comment per NOT-DERIVED page; checker_needles() :164-183; the coverage print
  :341-356.
- notes/scripts/measure_templates.py:70-72 coverage() calls b.checker_needles() directly; :121-124
  sets r["needles"]; :162 prints the per-page row; :175 prints "needles derived N of 17".
- notes/scripts/render_reports.py:2337 renders the census row's needles cell.
- notes/templates.md:14 and :80 prose; census rows :19-35 (16 NOT DERIVED, 1 derived).

Checkers that export phrase functions with no module-level population() (the derivable set):
verify_abstracts.py:129, verify_sources.py:140, verify_index_design.py:64 + :215,
verify_named_results.py:217, verify_verification_dirs.py:207, verify_t0_chains.py:112, and
verify_named_conjectures.py:65 (population(rows) — needs an argument-free form).

Pages whose checker exports no phrase functions at all stay NOT DERIVED by design (links.md,
dependency-drift.md, scope-exclusions.md, topics.md, subfinding-pairs.md, README.md, templates.md,
names.md, proof-density.md); their comments in ALL_PAGES must stay accurate.

Acceptance:
1. Every checker that exports count_phrases/size_phrases also exports a module-level population()
   that main() calls, so the builder derives its needles; no checker's checks get weaker.
2. The builder's report prints a real "checker needles N slotted X literal Y" line for each of those
   pages and keeps NOT DERIVED only for the pages whose checker exports no phrase functions.
3. notes/templates.md's needles column and the "needles derived N of 17" line match the builder, and

Decisions recorded during this bead:
- `notes/scripts/render_reports.py` is the writer for all four pages; `catlib/measure.py` carries the
  shared phrase-formatting. Checkers deliberately do not import it — a checker that re-derives a count
  through the same code as the page it checks proves nothing. Recorded in that module's docstring.
- The template's slot set IS the writer's slot dict. `build_report_templates.py` builds labels from
  `render_reports.py`'s own four slot functions, never from the page checker's needle list. The first
  version slotted the abstracts checker's 53 needles against the writer's 41 labels; Jinja renders an
  unknown key as the empty string, so the page silently lost 12 phrases and the render exited 0. The
  checker's needles are now read for a coverage line only, and print `NOT DERIVED` when the checker's
  `count_phrases` needs a population the builder does not have — a 0-needle report reads as green and
  checks nothing.
- Raw wrapping has two byte traps. Jinja captures a raw block's body verbatim, `trim_blocks` included,
  so `{% raw %}` on its own line EMITS the newline after it (every wrapped run gains a blank line),
  and `{%- raw %}` strips ALL preceding whitespace, deleting the blank line of a
  "heading, blank, LaTeX paragraph" run. The builder glues the tag to the run's first line, which
  consumes nothing. The flush test keys on the builder's own markers (`{{ p['`, `{% raw %}`,
  `{% endraw %}`, `{#`), not on any `{{`: `sources.md` quotes `\item{{{\ttfamily\char\`\\documentclass}`
  and `\def\extractclass#1#2@{%`, and flushing on those leaves the line unescaped —
  `TemplateSyntaxError: unexpected char '\'`.
- A phrase the page wraps across a line break is slotted only when the writer supplies it as split
  labels (`" a"`/`" b"`, which carry the break as the separator). A single-label phrase is left literal
  when its span contains a newline: slotting it drops the page's line break and reflows the paragraph.
  `sources.md` slots 28 of its 31 labels; the other 3 stay literal, byte-exact from HEAD.
- A label whose phrase is a substring of another label's phrase is dropped as `covered by` (the wider
  span already slots it); only a partial overlap is a hard error. Two cases: `union figure` inside
  `union verdict` (named-results), `single-root singleton count` inside `substring multi-root count`
  (sources).
- `render_reports.py` ended with a bare module-level `main()`, so `import render_reports as R` in the
  builder rendered and wrote all four pages as an import side effect. Fixed with
  `if __name__ == "__main__": main()`. The gate is unaffected — it runs the writer as `__main__`.
- `build_report_templates.py` is **not** gate-eligible: it rebuilds from `git show HEAD:<page>`, so a
  gate run would rewrite the templates from committed bytes. Run it with 0 args (all four pages) or 2

title: Fix the vacuous SLUG needle in verify_upstream_history.py
description:
# Fix the vacuous SLUG needle in `verify_upstream_history.py`

## Finding (measured 2026-10-09)

`verify_upstream_history.py`'s `SLUG` pattern is:

```
`([A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9-]*-(?:Jan|Feb|Mar|Apr|May|Jun|Jul|Aug|Sep|Oct|Nov|Dec)-\d{1,2}-\d{4})/`
```

It requires a trailing `/` inside the backticks. Measured over the three pages it checks, it matches
**0** tokens:

| Page | `SLUG` matches | Backticked slug-shaped tokens |
|---|---|---|
| `upstream_history/2026-10-07_3014888.md` | 0 | 14 |
| `upstream_history/2026-10-07_fd4aeeb.md` | 0 | 0 |
| `upstream_history/README.md` | 0 | 0 |

The 14 tokens are manuscript directory slugs with the date suffix, written in backticks with no
trailing slash — `Gaussian-free-field-limits-of-weighted-integer-Lipschitz-heights-October-6-2026`,
`Taming-implies-compatibility-on-four-manifolds-October-6-2026`, and 12 more, at
`upstream_history/2026-10-07_3014888.md:104-117`. The check is **vacuous, not failing**: the run exits
0 because nothing is asserted, and a mutant that renames one of those slugs is not caught by this
needle.

`math-lon.2.5` ported the file onto `catlib` and left the pattern untouched — its acceptance is
byte-identical gate reports, and widening a needle is a behavior change, not a port.

## Second finding (measured 2026-10-09): the needle is doubly vacuous

Dropping the trailing `/` is **necessary but not sufficient**. The month alternation is 3-letter and
the corpus writes **full month names only**. Bisect on one real token:

| pattern | result |
|---|---|
| `` `([A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9-]*)` `` | matches |
| `` `([A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9-]*-\d{4})` `` | matches |
| `` `([A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9-]*-October-\d{1,2}-\d{4})` `` | matches |
| `` `([A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9-]*-(?:Jan|...|Dec)-\d{1,2}-\d{4})` `` | **no match** |

`Oct` is followed by `t`, not by the `-` the pattern requires, and the alternation cannot backtrack
past it. Month forms over the **749** `preprints/` dirs: `September` 576, `October` 172, 1 no-match.
With full month names and no trailing slash the needle matches **14** tokens on
`2026-10-07_3014888.md` and **0** on the other two pages — exactly the bead's target.

## Work

1. Fix `SLUG` in **two** places: drop the trailing `/` (or make it optional) **and** widen the month
   alternation to the full names (`January|February|March|April|May|June|July|August|September|October|November|December`).
   Re-measure: the needle must match the 14 tokens on `2026-10-07_3014888.md` and 0 on the other two
   pages.
2. Add a mutant that renames one of the 14 slugs to a slug the release does not name, and confirm the
   run flags it. The mutant count rises from 12 to 13. With the current needle such a mutant would be
   vacuous — it passes because nothing is checked, which is the trap this step exists to avoid.
3. Sweep every doc that quotes the upstream-history mutant count: `notes/linting.md` (the `W0613` row
   anchors `verify_upstream_history.py:272,335` — line numbers move when the needle changes),
   `notes/scripts/README.md`, and the `.qwen/tmp/n5d3-draft.md` decision ledger.
4. Re-run the full gate twice; every other report must stay byte-identical.

## Acceptance

`python3 notes/scripts/verify_upstream_history.py` exits 0 and reports 14 slug matches;
`--mutant` exits 0 with the slug-rename mutant caught (13 of 13); the rest of the gate reports are
byte-identical to the pre-change reports.
close_reason: Fixed the vacuous SLUG needle in verify_upstream_history.py. Both halves measured: the trailing / inside the backticks and the 3-letter month alternation (the corpus writes full month names -- September 576, October 172 over the 749 preprints/ dirs), so the needle matched 0 tokens on all three pages and the run reported green while asserting nothing. With the slash optional and the full month names it matches 14 tokens on 2026-10-07_3014888.md (lines 104-117) and 0 on the other two pages, all 14 resolving to real preprints/ directories. Added the slug-rename mutant (12 -> 13) with the SLUG-pass-only needle ": slug '"; --mutant fires 13 of 13. The report now prints "slug tokens checked: 14" and a run that matches 0 is recorded as a problem, so a needle that matches nothing cannot report green again. Docs swept in the same pass: AGENTS.md, notes/README.md (13 injected faults), notes/linting.md (W0613 anchors :272,335 -> :275,338), notes/scripts/README.md (open finding -> fixed). Gate run twice: 62 invocations per run, all exit 0, run/md5/git diffs 0 bytes.

title: Project venv with jinja2, mypy, ruff, pylint; get notes/scripts passing them
description:
# Project venv with jinja2, mypy, ruff, pylint; get notes/scripts passing them

Nothing in `notes/scripts/` is type-checked or linted, and jinja2 is not installed (system Python is
PEP 668 externally managed, so installs need a venv).

## Goal
- A venv (untracked) with jinja2, mypy, ruff, pylint.
- `ruff` clean over `notes/scripts/`; `mypy` run with recorded per-file status; `pylint` warnings
  triaged, not necessarily zero.
- A tracked page recording the commands and the remaining exemptions.
- Prerequisite for the jinja2 templating bead (math-a0r).
close_reason: venv at .venv/ (uv-managed, untracked, CPython 3.12.13) with jinja2 3.1.6, mypy 2.4.0, ruff 0.16.10, pylint 4.1.2 / astroid 4.3.4; .venv/ gitignored. All three linters exit 0 over notes/scripts/ (44 files): ruff 446 findings at defaults -> 287 after the config -> 26 with --fix --unsafe-fixes -> 0 by hand; mypy 3 -> 0; pylint 1,422 -> 142 after the config -> 38 after the ruff autofixes -> 21 by hand -> 0 with three codes exempted (C0206 16, C0200 4, R0902 1). Configs at the repo root: ruff.toml, mypy.ini, .pylintrc, each exemption carrying the count it covers and a reason. notes/linting.md records the commands, versions, baseline, mypy per-file status (gate 44 files 0 errors with check_untyped_defs = False; strict probe --check-untyped-defs = 168 errors in 37 files, 7 clean) and the pylint triage. title: Refactor notes/scripts into a shared measurement package
description:
# Refactor notes/scripts into a shared measurement package

40 scripts in `notes/scripts/` re-derive the same joins: parse `overview.tex`, read
`notes/catalog.tsv`, resolve manuscript dirs, read `lean/formalization.yaml`, walk `preprints/`.
The 2026-10-07 merge showed the cost: every script carries its own copy of a rule, so a corpus
change breaks 13 checkers at once, and a signature change in `extract_links.py` broke
`verify_t0_chains.py`.

## Goal
One importable package under `notes/scripts/` that owns the corpus measurement, with the per-page
checkers reduced to page logic + mutants.

## Sub-beads
- `math-pkg.1` — the package: ledger reading, overview parsing, preprint path resolution, yaml
  reading, Lean tree walking; move duplicated helpers out of the extractors.
- `math-pkg.2` — port every `verify_*` checker to the package; mutant lists must not shrink.
- `math-pkg.3` — promote the useful scratch scripts, delete the unused ones, record the inventory.
close_reason: All three sub-beads closed. math-lon.1 ships catlib (paths, text, ledger, overview, preprints, tsv, yaml, anchors); math-lon.2 ports all 19 verify_* checkers to it (32 of 44 scripts import it; gate byte-identical across the port, mutant counts unchanged); math-lon.3 ships the inventory page with class, target and gate command for every script plus the scratch location rule. Remaining scratch promotion and deletion is math-8ou, which the inventory page and AGENTS.md now name.

title: Render generated notes files from jinja2 templates so counts cannot drift
description:
# math-a0r epic conversion (proposal, drafted 2026-10-09 before claiming)

`math-a0r` is a 6-step plan in one bead. Per the standing directive ("before beginning any large
bead, consider converting it to an epic and doing the work in sub-beads"), convert it to an epic and
create the sub-beads below. **Dependency direction, measured 2026-10-09:** a sub-bead cannot block the
epic at all — `bd create --deps blocks:math-a0r` on a child prints
`failed to add dependency math-a0r.1 -> math-a0r: epics can only block other epics, not tasks`, and a
child created *as a blocker of* the epic becomes the blocker itself. The hierarchy is carried by
`--parent` alone, and the epic gates on its children through bd's own child gate
(`--waits-for-gate all-children`), so the sub-beads ship with **no** explicit dependency edges.

| Sub-bead | Work | Gate |
|---|---|---|
| `.1` | **Already shipped** — verify and record the orphan sweep `build_index.py:763-776` does (unlink files not in `WRITTEN`, rmdir empty dirs, print `stale swept`); record it in the bead and the docs as the precondition of `.3` | `build_index.py` twice: report identical, tree byte-identical; `check_index_links.py` exits 0 with 0 broken; report reads `stale swept 0 files [] empty dirs removed 0` |
| `.2` | Measurement API: one module returning the measured population as a dict (the `build_catalog` joins + the per-page measurements the checkers re-derive) | imports from a script need `sys.path.insert(0, "notes/scripts")`; every existing caller keeps its output |
| `.3` | Template the fully generated tree: `build_index.py`'s page builders → `notes/templates/*.j2` | rendered tree byte-identical to committed `notes/index/` (1,049 files) |
| `.4` | Template the 4 densest report-fed pages: `index-design.md` (82 phrases), `named-results.md` (66), `abstracts.md` (45), `sources.md` (31) | each page renders byte-identically; its checker keeps its full mutant list |
| `.5` | Template the remaining report-fed pages (`counterexample-crosscheck`, `t0-chains`, `subfinding-pairs`, `scope-exclusions`, `dependency-drift`, `verification-dirs`, `topics`, `links`, `proof-density`, `names`, `index-links`, `README`) | same gate per page |
| `.6` | Re-scope the checkers (render-to-temp diff replaces the count-phrase literal match; quotations/anchor mutants unchanged) + docs sweep + tracked template inventory page + the simulated ledger-bump demo | full gate twice, byte-identical; a scratch copy with one changed ledger count propagates by re-render alone |

Non-goals stay as written in the bead: no templating of reading records, no checker deletions,
`topics.tsv` / `conjecture-standing.tsv` keep their hand-authored columns.

Count reconciliation for `.3`: the committed tree is **1,049** files (`build_index.py` report: 1,033
pages + 16 tables); the bead's inventory says **1,036** `.md` because it was measured 2026-10-08,
before the orphan sweep — the 3-file difference is exactly the three orphan pages the sweep deletes.
`.1` is therefore the precondition of `.3`, not a parallel task.

Constraint discovered while drafting: claiming a bead writes `.beads/issues.jsonl`, which moves
`git status` between the driver's two snapshots. Claim only after the gate finishes and the commits
land, so `gate_git_diff` stays 0 bytes.
acceptance_criteria: build_index.py run twice: report identical + tree byte-identical + check_index_links.py exits 0 with 0 broken; every templated page renders byte-identically to its committed content; no typed count literal remains in the templated pages; every checker in the templated set still flags its full mutant list; a simulated ledger count change propagates by re-render alone
close_reason:
math-a0r closed (epic, 7 sub-beads).

Goal: render the generated notes files from jinja2 templates so a count cannot drift between a page
and the code that measures it.

Sub-beads:
- `.1` the shipped orphan sweep in `build_index.py` verified and recorded (precondition of `.3`).
- `.2` the measurement API — `catlib/measure.py`, counts as data with no report formatting.
- `.3` `build_index.py`'s page builders templated into `notes/templates/index/` (5 skeletons).
- `.4` the 4 densest report-fed pages templated (`index-design`, `named-results`, `abstracts`,

title: Decide the prettier scope and apply it to our markdown
description:
The pilot formatted AGENTS.md in place and the emphasis question is answered; the
file scope is not chosen. Prettier 3.9.9 is pinned in package.json.

Scope by ownership. Ours (49 files): AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, notes/*.md (26),
notes/summaries/** (21). Never format: notes/index/** (1,034 generated pages -
edit the generator), preprints/** and lean/** (release mirror), root README.md and
CONTENTS.md (release mirror), .beads/README.md (bd-generated),
.qwen/skills/**/SKILL.md (YAML frontmatter).

Measured prettier 3.9.9 behavior (pilot + 49-file shadow tree, not assumed):
* x * -> _x_ unconditionally - the markdown printer's option registry is only
{proseWrap, singleQuote}, so emphasisStar and tableSpacing are rejected as unknown
options; __c__ -> **c**; tables padded; padding stripped inside double-backtick
spans; embeddedLanguageFormatting:"off" keeps code fences verbatim; proseWrap:
"preserve" keeps our line wrapping; **strong**, backtick counts and "- " bullets
are unchanged; code spans are immune, so a checker's own quoted pattern in a code
span survives while prose emphasis does not. Two non-cosmetic behaviors: a list
continuation line can be emitted at column 0, detaching the tail of a list item,
and a prose continuation line starting with "+ " is read as a bullet and rewritten
to "- " with the rest of the paragraph re-indented (2 such lines in our scope).
Restore is not stable: converting _x_ back to *x* and re-running prettier
reproduces the formatted file byte-for-byte, so a format+restore workflow leaves
files that fail prettier --check.

Checker damage over the 21 summary pages (baseline 3589 markers, 940 spans, 0
problems, 0 undetected mutants): 29 real-page Pass C quote failures over 13 pages,
which disables the mutant gate on those pages (26 undetected mutants). Cause 1:
_x_ inside a quotation - norm() strips ** * and backticks but not _. Cause 2:
blank-line insertion around block quotes moves Pass C's "citation on the line
above" window. 5 checkers key on the literal *"..."* form and 4 use strict
single-space table regexes. 589 of the run's Pass B problems were an artifact of
symlinked release dirs in the shadow tree, not prettier.

Options put to the user: A format only the 5 files no script reads (AGENTS.md,
CLAUDE.md, notes/conjecture-standing.md, notes/proof-density.md,
notes/summaries-workflow.md); B format all 49 and adapt every checker
(emphasis-pair-scoped _ stripping in each norm(), widen the 5 *"..."* patterns,
relax the 4 table regexes); C format all 49 with a tracked restore post-pass
(breaks --check); D downgrade prettier. Config in every variant: proseWrap
"preserve" plus embeddedLanguageFormatting "off", shipped as its own tracked
.prettierrc commit.
notes: DECISION (2026-10-08): restore, not adapt. Prettier 3.9.9 formatted 47 notes/ markdown files (2927+/2878-); the plain checker run then failed 7 checkers with 79 real problems (41 verify_summaries, 30 verify_t0_chains, 4 verify_named_conjectures, 1 each verify_abstracts/verify_index_design/verify_named_results, 1 pre-existing verify_findings) and the mutant run failed 12, the dominant class being mutants that can no longer be injected. Mechanisms: norm() strips **/*/backticks/HTML/LaTeX but not _; strict table regexes require | n | with no padding; *"…" quote patterns; block-quote attribution windows. Byte rewrites measured from the diff: 720 _x_ spans, 244 *"…" -> _"…" (5 survivors, all in code spans), 2,043 padded table lines. Unconfigurable: the markdown printer registry is proseWrap + singleQuote only. Restored with git checkout -- notes/ at 57c6cf08b; 17 of 18 checkers green on both runs. Scope recorded in .prettierignore: prettier applies only to the 4 pages no checker parses (conjecture-standing, links, proof-density, summaries-workflow).
close_reason: Scope decided and enforced: prettier limited to the 4 checker-unread pages; the 43 byte-exact pages restored and excluded in .prettierignore.
